(Wlm.) mí-a ~ míz-a [ Rn.] = mizz-ā “vacca” [Crl.] = mizz-a “cow” [Alm.] = mīz-a “livestock, cattle” [ LS 1997, 477], Malo mīs-a “bue” [CR], Zala mizz-ā “vacca” [CR] = miz-ā “vacca” [Crl.] = miz-a “cow” [ Lmb.], Gofa mizz-ā “vacca” vs. mis-ē “bue” [CR, Crl.] = miz-a “cow” [ Lmb.], Gamu mīz-i ~ mīz-a “cow” [ Lmb.], Dawro miz-a “cow” [Alm.], Doko mīse “bue” [CR], Dorze mīz “cow” [Alm.] (NWOmt.: Alm. 1993, 6, #148) | SEOmt. *mīs- “cow” [ Bnd.]: Zys. mis-ō “vacca” [Crl.] = mīs [Sbr.], Zrg. mīs “cow” [Sbr.], Koyra (Bdt.) mis-ā “vacca sterile” vs. mis-ē “bue” [Crl.] = miz-a “ox” [ Lmb.] = mīsε “cow” [Sbr.], Haruro (Kcm.) mis “vacca” [CR] = mīs “cow” [Sbr.], Ganjule mis [Sbr.] (SEOmt.: Sbr. 1994, 13) | Chara miy-ā [*-z-] “vacca” [Crl.] | Jnj. (Yemsa) miy-ā [*-z-] “vacca” [Crl.] = mìǯà “cow” [Aklilu n.d. MS, #148] | Sns. mīz-ā “vacca” [Crl.], Wambera mīz-a “cow” [ Flm.], Bworo miz-o “cow” [ Flm.] (NOm.: Rn. 1888, 318; CR 1927, 249; 1936, 655; Crl. 1929, 33, 50, 62; 1938 III, 80, 115, 173, 206; 1951, 471–473; Flm. 1987, 146, §5; Lmb. 1993, 100, 106; Bnd. 2003, 115, #31 & 162) ||| ECh.: Barein múúzo “Ochse” [ Lks. 1937, 51] = (misquoted as Birgit!) muuzo “ox” [OS] | Birgit múuséy (f ) “biche” [ Jng. 2004, 357]. ■ 3. GT: or perhaps cp. Ch. *maʒ(VH)- “kind of antelope” [Stl.] = *maHʒ- “1. antelope, 2. goat” [GT ]: WCh.: Hausa mààzóó ~ mààǯíí “harnessed antelope (Tragelophus scriptus)” [Abr. 1962, 672, 640] | Mburku maazu “antelope sp.” [Skn. 1996, not in Skn. 1977] | Mangas (from Hs.) màazoo “harness antelope” [Csp. 1994, 40], Zul (from Hs.) maazóo [Csp. 1994, 237] | (?) Bade mázàrə̀n (compound?) “Ziegenbock” [ Lks. 1968, 224] || CCh.: Fali-Bwagira munza-ḫwun [< var. *manz-?] “male goat” [Skn.] | Ktk. *mʌzʌ “Antilopa hamariya” [ Prh. 1972, 64, #38.2]: Logone mázā, pl. mázē-n “Antilope Hamaraya” [ Lks. 1936, 108] = maza “femelle du Cob de Buffon (Adenota cob Erxleben)” [ Lbf. 1976, 18] | Mtk. múzàk “he-goat” [ Rsg. 1978, 260, #312], perhaps Gsg. mazawal (compound?) “male goat” [Skn.] (Ch.: Skn. 1996, 200)? ■ 4. GT: Akk. (mA) maʔišu “eine Schafrasse (?)” [AHW 586] = “(a breed of sheep)” [CAD m1, 116] or MSA: Jbl. mŝy: moŝέt “livestock” [ Jns. 1981, 175] are probably out of question.

notes.label: ap
notes.text: H. G. Mukarovsky (1987, 135) compared NOm. *mizz- with Mande “cow, cattle”: NMande mìsi ~ nisi, Mandinka nìnsi, Xassonke ny�nsi, Bambara mìsí, Jula misí.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The etymology of NOm. *m�īz- “cow” [ Mlt.] is highly disputed: (1) There seems to be a great confusion in the handling of the reflexes of NOm. miz- “Rind” (above) and NOm. *minǯ- “cattle” [GT ]: Gofa mínǯ-o “Rind” [ Rn.] | Kefoid *minǯ- [GT ]: Kaffa minǯ-ō “bestiame bovino (?)”, cf. minǯ-ifō “sterco di bovini” [Crl.] = minǯ-o “cattle” [ Lmb.], Sns. minǯ-ā [d’Abbadie/Crl.] = minǯ-ō “vacca” [ Beke/Crl.] = mīnz-a “cattle” [ Lmb.], Anf. mints-ō “bestiame bovino” [Crl.] = mints-o “cow, cattle” [ Flm., Lmb.], Guba minz-a “cow, head of cattle” [ Flm.], Naga minǯ-o “id.” [ Flm.] (Kefoid: Flm. 1987, 146, §5) | Sheko mīnǯ-o “cows, cattle” [ Lmb.] (NOm.: Lmb. 1993, 106). The reflexes of both NOm. roots are usually mentioned together in Omotic etymologies by L. Reinisch (1888, 318), E. Cerulli (1929, 33; 1938 III 80; 1951, 471–2), H. Fleming (1987, 146), M. Lamberti (1993, 100, 106) as if the coll. NOm. *minǯ- “cattle” had derived from a reduplication (*mimǯ- < *mimz-?) of NOm. *miz-. On the other hand, NOm. *minǯ- “cattle” (palatalized < *ming-?) is fairly close to ES: Amh. mänga, Gafat mänga “flock, herd”, which Praetorius (1879, 169) derived from *nhg “to guide, conduct”, while D. Appleyard (1977, 26/68) prefers a Cushitic borrowing, cf. LECu.: Afar mang-o “herd” < mag- be full”. (2) L. Reinisch (1888, 318) equated the NOm. root with Cpt. ⲙⲁⲥⲉ, ⲙⲉⲥⲓ “bos vitulus”. Incorrect both phonologically and semantically, the underlying Eg. being msj “to bear (child)”. (3) H. G. Mukarovsky (1987, 135) compared it with Sha nísí mú rà�óŋ “Kuh” [ Jng. 1970, 288], which is false, since the latter lit. means “female of cattle”, cf. Sha nísí “weiblich” [ Jng.]. (4) M. Lamberti (1993, 100; 1993, 355; LS 1997, 473–4) derived Wlt. mīza, Sns. mīnz-a (treating the sibilant as a “formative suffix”) from an OCu. (Cu.-Om.) *māl- “to milk” (sic). The segmentation of -z- is unfounded. Moreover, the shift of Om. *-n- < older *-l- cannot be accepted on historical phonological grounds. A similar position has been taken by Philippson (2003 MS, 3) who assumed “an -s- increment” added to a root *mī- attested in Chara & Yemsa mi(y)-, Kafa mīm-, Mao: Sezo & Hozo ʔim(m)-, which is equally dubious, since the shift of *-z- > -y- is well known in NOm., while the Mao form represents a distinct root. (5) V. É. Orel & O. V. Stolbova (1992, 182; HSED #1809) ECh.: Birgit mūzo “ox” combine with Eg. mḏ.t (coll.) “stalled cattle” (MK, FD 123) = “Vieh, Herde” (Wb II 185). Incorrect both phonologically and semantically (rejected already by G. Takács 1996, 443, #6.1; 1996, 140). Orel and Stolbova ignored that MEg. mḏ.t “stalled cattle” is a secondary meaning developed from OEg. mḏ.t “byre” (FD 123) = “Viehhof, Stall” (OK, Wb II 185). Moreover, Eg. -ḏ vs. ECh.: Birgit -ǯ seem irregular. (6) A. Militarev (SED II 200–1, #148) affiliated NOm. “cow” with the reflexes (denoting “goat” and “antelope”) of his AA *maʕi(n)ʒ- “kind of ungulate” (see below).

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: Cf. also Sem. *ma/iʕ(a)z- “goat” [SED]: OSA: Min. (Mdb.) mʕzy (dual, hapax) “chèvre” [Arbach 1993, 59], Safaitic mʕzy “Ziegen” [Sima], Ar. maʕz- ~ maʕaz- “nom gén.: chèvres et boucs, espèce, race caprine”, māʕiz- “(masc. et fem.) chèvre ou bouc, pièce du troupeau de l’espèce caprine”, miʕzāʔ- ~ miʕāz- ~ maʕīz- “chèvre ou bouc”, ʔamʕūz- “1. chèvre ou bouc, 2. troupe de gazelles ou de chamois”, etc. [ BK II 1127, cf. Lane 2724], Yemeni Ar. maʕaz, maʕiz, miʕz (coll.) “Ziegen” [ Behnstedt 1985, 210, 213] (Sem.: Hommel 1879, 243; Kogan 2000, 1, #2; Sima 2000, 116–7; SED II 200–1, #148) < AA *m-(ʕ)-ʒ “1. antelope, 2. goat” [GT ]? In this case, a shift of OEg. mjz.t < *mʕz.t (incompatible) would have to be accounted for.

notes.label: lit
notes.text: Skn. 1977, 191 (Ar.-Ch.); SED II 200–1 (Sem.-Ch.-NOm.). A. Militarev (2005, 87) considers Sem. *ma/iʕ(a)z- as a mV- prefix formation from Sem. *ʕVnz- “goat” [SED II #35]. L. Kogan (SED l.c.) treats JA mēʕazzē, mēʕazzəyā, məʕizzē, məʕizzayyā “from goats, goats-hair, horn etc.” [ Jastrow 1950, 814] = “was von Ziegen kommt, Ziegenhaar u. dgl., caprinum” [ Levy 1924 III 185] as reflexes of the same PSem. stem with a “secondary derivation” (adopted also in Sem. lexicography) from Sem. *ʕVnz- “goat” (via the synchronic analysis of JA mēʕazzē < *min-ʕazzē “from goats”), which, in his view, “can be only a popular etymology”. Kogan explained Ar. mirʕizz- ~ mirʕizzā “poil fin, duvet sous le poil plus gros (chez les chèvres)” [ BK I 881] as a possible Aramaism.

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: Note that N. Skinner has divided the Bade word as mázà-rə̀n contra Lukas: mázàr-ə̀n.

notes.label: nb3
notes.text: Following O. V. Stolbova (1996, 115), A. Militarev (SED l.c.) equated the Chadic forms with the isogloss of ECh.: Bdy. máḍay “gazelle ourebi” [AJ 1989, 96] ||| SCu.: Dhl. máʕaḏe “female topi” [ Ehret 1980, 156, #24 with false comparanda] = máʕa�e “female kudu” [ EEN 1989, 36], which seems phonologically problematic (Bdy. -ḍ- < *-Hd- < *-Hʒ- and Dhl. -ḏ- < *-ʒ- not proven), cf. also WCh.: Jimi maado “goat” [Gowers/JI ], Zaar màaḍ “goat” [Smz. 1975, 29] || ECh.: EDng. máḍíyá & WDng. màḍìyà (f ) “la gazelle, le Cob de Buffon (plus petite que ḅòtìlā)” [ Dbr.-Mnt. 1973, 192], Bdy. máḍay (f ) “gazelle ourébi” [AJ 1989, 96] | Mkl. mòḍó (f ) “Ziege”, mòḍú (m) “Ziegenbock” [ Lks. 1977, 225] = mòḍú (m), mòḍó (f ) “bouc, chèvre” [ Jng. 1990, 140] (Ch.: JI 1994 II 166–7), which can be better explained from PCh. *m-ḍ “goat” [ JI 1994 I 80] < AA *m-ʕ-d “1. gazelle, 2. goat” [GT ]. Note that CCh.: Masa m�-da “goat” [ Mch.] derives from Ch. *m- [ JI l.c.].

notes.label: nb4
notes.text: A. Militarev (SED II 200–1, #148) affiliated also NOm. *m�īz- “cow” (see above) with the reflexes of his AA *maʕi(n)ʒ- “kind of ungulate” (denoting “goat” and “antelope”). NB5: SCu.: Dhl. mṓǯo “eland, greater kudu” [ EEN 1989, 38] = mōǯo (mōdʒo) “sp. large antelope” [ MSSL 1993, 40, #102] cannot belong here, being a late loan-word from SNil. (as suggested by EEN l.c.).

text: mjz.t “Leber” (PT, Wb II 44, 11) = “liver” (FD 105; cf. AEO II 245*–249*, §598) = “Leber (Mensch, Tier)” (GHWb 326; ÄWb I 513–5). ● Hence: Dem. mws “Leber” (DG 157) → OCpt. ⲙⲁⲟⲩⲥⲉ ~ ⲙⲁⲟⲩⲥⲓ “an internal organ: (?) liver” (CED 95; AEO II 245*; exx. apud Richter 1998, 138) = “ein inneres Organ, wohl: Leber” (KHW 107) = “(prob.) foie” (DELC 127) = “ein Organ in der Bauchhöhle: Leber (?)” (Spg. KHW 68: cf. Griffith, ZÄS 38, 1900, 92). ● There can be hardly any doubt that it is identical with NOm. *mayz- “liver” [ Blz.] = *māyz- [ Ehret]: NWOmt. *māyz- [ Bnd.]: Male māyzi [ Bnd.] = maizi [Sbr. 1994–95, 9] = mayz [ Flm./Blz.], Bsk. māyız [ Bnd.] = mayz [ Flm.] = māyiz [ Mlt.], Doko mayz [ Flm.] (NWOmt.: Bnd. 2000 MS, 58, #81) | SEOmt. *mayy- [reg. from *mayz-]: Haruro (Kcm.) māy-ē [CR 1936, 655] = may-e [ Bnd.] = mayy-e [ Flm.] = māy-e [ LS] = maǯ-e [Sbr.], Kyr. mayy-e [ Flm. 1990, 28] = māy-e [ Bnd.] = māyy-ε [Sbr.], Gdc. māyy-e [ Bnd.], Gnj. may-e [ Blz. < ?], Zrg. ma’y-e [ Bnd.] = mā-e [Sbr.], Zys. ma’y-e [ Bnd.] = ma-ē [Sbr.] = māy-a [ LS] | Chara mayy-a [ Flm.] | Benesho may (“heart”) [ Flm.], She mai [ Bnd.] (NOm.: Bnd. 1971, 254–6, 261; Bnd.-Flm. 1976, 50; Mkr. 1981, 203, #20; Blz. 1989 MS Om., 21, #72; Sbr. 1994, 17; Dlg. 1998, 59, #69) < AA *mayʒ- “liver” [ Dlg.]. Note that LECu.: Bussa máyē “liver” [ Wdk.-Tanaba-Cheru 1994, 12, #47] may be a NOm. borrowing. ● All other etymologies offered for OEg. mjz.t are unconvincing: ■ 1. H. Brugsch (quoted by Horrack 1894, 143–4) assumed a connection to Eg. jmstj “einer der vier Horussöhne, Schutzgott der Eingeweide” (OK, Wb I 88) based on the old (false) rendering of mjz.t as “great intestine” (Chabas) = “(perhaps act. some) internal organ of the animals body, perhaps the stomach” (Horrack). ■ 2. H. Grapow (1914, 23), P. Lacau (1970 phon., 39, §19; 1970, 150, #406), and W. Vycichl (1983, 127) supposed an m- prefix in Eg. mjz.t, but they were unable to identify the root (*jz ~ *wjz or sim.), which mjz.t might have originated in. ■ 3. GT: assuming an orig. OEg. mrz.t (suggested by Roquet and others, quoted above), one might ponder comparing it with Ch. *m-[l]-d “liver” [ JS 1981, 167]: CCh.: BM *m-ḍ “liver” [GT ] > Chibak miḍæ, Ngwahyi miḍà, WMargi miḍà, miḍəgə̀ (CCh.: Krf. 1981, #70) || ECh.: Sokoro meíld-ụm “deine Leber” [ Lks. 1937, 36]. But the correspondence of Ch. *-d vs. OEg. -z is irregular.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The word occurs in great number of instances in the OK offering lists, mostly written the alphabetical signs m + z, where no -r- (!) was written (ÄWb I 513–5). We also know that the hrgl. mj (W19) had already lost its old mr value (Kahl 1994, 801, W19: value mj already in the archaic period, cf. also FÄW 176–177) by that time when they began to write mjz.t “liver” occasionally with W19 too, let alone the common and well-attested erosion of old r > j in the OK (AÄG 56, §128). G. Roquet (1979, 442–3, 437–8) brings two exx., in which the -r- was written alphabetically, namely late OK (Dyn. V offering list) mrz.t and CT I 289c (T1C) mrz.t, which are hardly sufficient for setting up an etymon *mrz.t (accepted also in NBÄ 695, n. 793; AL 79.1164; Peust 1999, 140), since even if there was formerly an -r- in our word, it must have certainly been long lost by the late OK and MK, and henceforth these two pseudohistorical forms hardly reflect the actual spelling of the word, which was written without the r sign everywhere else during the OK (numerous exx. listed in ÄWb l.c.). In spite of CT I 289c (T1C) mrz.t, a number of recent standard works (DCT 162 & 174; Kahl 1992, 111) stick to assuming OK mjz.t. Similarly rightly assumes W. Westendorf (1962, 32–33) the OK wtg. mz.t to be a defective form of mjz.t. P. Kaplony (1974, 224) finds only mjz.t in Abusir. The problem of *mrz.t strikingly resembles the phenomenon observed, e.g., with the OEg. root bnj, where usually a process of old bnr > later bnj is accepted. As shown, however, by W. Vycichl (1951, 71; 1978, 73; 1983, 29), W. Schenkel (1965, 114–115), and H. Satzinger (1999, 144, fn. 8), the original root might have been bnj (OK when -r does not appear in most cases), which was replaced then by a false bnr in the later times (MK) due to a “pseudohistorization” (Vycichl 1951) or “archaizing orthography ( graphie archaïsante)” (Vycichl 1983) or “hypercorretcion” (Satzinger). By analogies (where the historic process of erosion of r > j indeed took place), the scribes of the MK might have felt bnj too as a development from an earlier *bnr (which actually never existed from an etymological viewpoint).

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: For the correction of (O) ⲙⲁⲟⲩⲥ (m) “liver” (cited in Wb l.c.; Lefébvre 1952, 33–34, §38; NBÄ 695, n. 793) to ⲙⲁⲟⲩⲥⲉ, cf. Vergote 1950, 291.

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: Cf. also the gloss ⲙⲟⲥⲉ “Leber” in a mag. Dem. pap. (Richter 1998, 137–9).

notes.label: nb3
notes.text: W. C. Till (1955, 331, §43) confirms the loss of the native Eg. word for “liver” by Coptic times, when it was replaced by Gk. 0παρ in medical texts.

notes.label: nb4
notes.text: J. Osing derived the Dem.-OCpt. form from *mě́jz.̆t (NBÄ 695, n. 793) leaving the anomaly of “the unexplained change of -j- > -w-” (AEO II 245*).

notes.label: ap
notes.text: H. G. Mukarovsky (1981, 203) compared the NOm. word with Nilo-Saharan: Teda maasen “liver”. M. L. Bender (1975, 172) combined Eg. mjz.t with Niger- Kordofanian: Igbo imeǯn “liver”. DP: A. Ju. Militarev (1991, 76) linked OEg. mjz.t to IE: Hitt. mazeri- ~ maze- “Teil der Orakelleber” [ Friedrich 1952, 139] as well as to NCauc.: Avar-Andi *mVc̣V “liver”, (?) PTsezi *bɔc̣ə “spleen” > i.a. Bezhti bac̣o “liver” (NCauc.: NCED 1040). A. Dolgopolsky (1994, 267, #1; 1994 MS, 3; 1998, 59, #69) affiliated AA *mayʒ- with Ur. *maksa “liver” < Nst. *magiʒa.

notes.label: lit
notes.text: the Eg.-NOm. etymology was first observed by Ch. Rabin (1977, 338) and (independently) also by Blz. 1989 MS Om., 21, #72 (Eg.-NOm.). See also Mlt. 1991, 76 (Eg.-Hitt.-NCauc.); Dlg. 1994, 267, #1 & 1994 MS, 3 & 1998, 59, #69 (Eg.-NOm.); Ehret 1997, 214, #1834 (Eg.-NOm.); Takács 1998, 158–9, #2; 2005, 22–23, §1.7 & fn. 16 (Eg.-NOm.-Igbo-NCauc.); Mlt. 2005, 344, 367 (Eg.-NOm.).

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: For the reason of historical phonology, the isogloss of Eg. mjz.t and NOm. *mayz- can hardly related to WCh.: SBch. *mbaŝ >/< *maŝ (?) “liver” [GT ] = *mb-s2 [ JS 1981, 168]: Mbaaru maasi [Smz.], Grnt. màasì [Smz.] = màasi [Csp.], Jimi bàaso [Csp.], Tala bàsì [Csp.], Zungur basì [Csp.], Boolu & Pelu mbaŝì [Smz.], Zangwal mbasí [Smz.], Sho mbasi [Smz.], Geji mba�ì [Smz.], Zaranda mbaŝì [Smz.], Buli & Polchi & Zodi (Dwot) mbaŝ [Smz.], Langas mbàŝ [Smz.], Tule & Chaari mba�ə̀ [Smz.], Zakshi bà�ə́ʔ [Smz.], Boot mba�ə [Smz.], Zaar (Saya) m̀bwoŝ [Smz.] (SBch.: Smz. 1978, 26, 49–50, #24; Csp. 1994, 24). The position of ECh.: Karbo messo “liver” [el-Minai n.d. MS] is uncertain. First, (1) the irregular Eg.-Om. *-z (< AA *ʒ) vs. SBauchi *-ŝ should be explained. Moreover, (2) SBch. *mbaŝ is presumably cognate with NAgaw: Qwara hebšā “Bauch, Leber” [ Rn. 1885, 75] = hibša (i.e. həbša) “liver” [Apl. 1991 MS, 8] = hebša “liver” vs. ḫebša “stomach” [ Flad apud Rn.], Falasha hebša “liver” [Apl. 1996, 16] (from an etymon *ḥVbš- with the AA prefix of anatomical terms?). The Sem. etymology apud L. Reinisch (l.c.) is dubious, while most recently D. Appleyard (2006, 94) offers no etymology for it at all.

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: Ch. Rabin (1977, 338) was inclined to identify the common Eg.-NOm. stem with ES: Geez māʔĕs “skin” [ Rabin] = māʔs ~ māʕs “skin, hide, leather, headcover” [ Lsl. 1987, 324] referring to the analogous parallelism of WCh.: Hausa hanta ~ anta “liver” and Geez anadā “skin” (rare). Phonologically dubious (AA *-Z > Eg.-NOm. *-z ≠ Geez -s). Besides, Geez māʔs “skin” might be related with Eg. *ms.t (q.v.).

notes.label: nb3
notes.text: Surprisingly, M. Lamberti & R. Sottile (1997, 476) equated NOm. *mayz- with NOm.: Wlt. miyyiy-a “rib” = HECu.: Kmb. mizāz-u “rib” & LECu.: Afar masangale “rib, side of the body” & Bed. biye “rib” & even Dhl. makk-o “liver” (sic).

notes.label: nb4
notes.text: Since the function of liver could have hardly been known in the PAA period, an eventual connection of AA *mayʒ- “liver” [ Dlg.] to the etymon of Ar. myz II “séparer, distinguer de” [ Fagnan 1923, 167] = I “séparer l’un d’avec l’autre”, II & IV “séparer, disjoindre l’un d’avec l’autre” [ BK II 1172] is rather unlikely.

notes.label: nb5
notes.text: The Eg.-NOm. etymology was queried by J. Osing (2001, 576 & fn. 106) uncritically adopting the reading of Eg. mjz.t as mrz.t suggested by G. Roquet (1979, 437–8, 442–3). His objection was disproved by G. Takács (2005, 22–23, §1.7).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: In the Canopic jars, mjz.t “liver” (with few exceptions) was indeed identified with Imsety (presiding over the embalmed viscera), but hardly because of a real etymological connection, “since paranomasia has here played an unmistakeable part” (AEO II 247*; Ghalioungui 1981, 15).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Lacau (1970 phon., 39, §19), suggesting a value ml-/mn- (sic) for the hrgl. mj < mr (W19), assumed an “unknown triradical root” (i.e., *l?z/*n?z). Unfounded.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The position of ECh.: Sarwa ngál-màndà, Gadang mùyò “liver” (both derived in JI 1990 MS, 6, #113 from Ch. *m-l-d) is uncertain. It has not been researched whether Gadang -y- can be < *-yy- < *-yz- (as in the case of NOm. *mayzabove).

text: mjz.wt (or mjzw.t?) “Name der weißen Krone, auch als Göttin” (PT, NK, GR, Wb II 44, 15–16) = “la couronne haute à la tête du roi du Sud” (Lefébvre 1893, 114) = “Southern Crown” (Blackman (1916, 69) = “couronne blanche” ( Jéquier 1921, 12) = “Name der oberägyptischen Königskrone” (PT 724b, 753b, ÜKAPT VI 130) = “un des noms de la couronne blanche” (Lacau 1970, 38) = “(klärlich) eine Krone als Ganzes (trotz abweichender Determinierung)” (Otto ÄMÖR II 134) = “white crown” (PL 412). ● Etymology obscure. ■ 1. H. Grapow (1914, 23) saw in it an m- prefix form, but failed to identify the underlying root. ■ 2. A. M. Blackman (1916, 69): since mjzw.t “produces assonance with” Eg. nsw “king” in PT 724a–b, it “is likewise a derivative of ” Eg. sw.t “eine Pflanze: Art Binse” (MK, Wb IV 58), “mj- being a prefix”. Similarly, P. Wilson (PL 412): “a connection with either swt or nswt seems possible”. False. ■ 3. P. Lacau (1970, 38 & fn. 2) suggested a “prototype” *m-nzw.t originating in OEg. nzw “roi du Haute Égypte” (see nsw) with a prefix m-, which later shifted to m-jzw.t with the rare change of Eg. n > j. In his view, mjzw.t is “à comparer sans doute avec métathèse le nom de couronne nws” (Lacau, RT 31, 1909, 30, l. 2 & 7). ■ 4. D. Meeks (AL 77.1658): lit. “la pointue” originating in Eg. mjz.(t) “la tige, la pointe arrière de la couronne rouge” (discussed above).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The segmentation is disputed. Mostly treated as mjzw.t. K. Sethe (ÜKAPT III 343) suggests an original form mjz.t.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: As rightly noted by A. H. Gardiner (quoted by Blackman 1916, 69, fn. 3, cf. RT 33, 75), mjzw.t cannot be a derivative of sw.t, as the hrgl. W19 is only used in m- formations when either the 1st radical is j- or when the 1st radical becomes j-.

gloss: Name der weißen Krone, auch als Göttin

text: mjs.wt (pl.? or mjsw.t as in Wb?) “eine Pflanze aus dem Wadi Natrûn” (Lit. MK: Peasant R 22, Wb II 45, 1). ● Meaning and origin unknown. GT: cf. perhaps Akk. mēsu or mēšu “a native tree and its wood” [CAD m2, 33] || NHbr. of TTM mayiš “1. Zürgelbaum (Celtis australis), 2. die Frucht dieses Baumes” [ Dalman 1922, 235] = “ein Baum der Eicheln und Galläpfel trägt” [ Levy 1924 III 100] = “a tall tree with fruits like myrtle-berries” [ Löw apud Jastrow] = “name of a tree, Celtis” [ Jastrow 1950, 772] | Ar. mays- “1. sorte d’arbre du bois duquel on fait des selles, 2. coll. selles” [ BK II 1173]?

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Mathieu (1996, 107, n. 355) found a further occurence (written mjsj < *mjs.t) in Ostr. DeM 1266 + CGC 25218, 15.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Levy (l.c.) compared a certain Cpt. ⲙⲏⲥ (unspecified).

gloss: eine Pflanze aus dem Wadi Natrûn

text: mjk.t (with vars.) “Göttin des Gebiets des 1. Katarakt, eng mit Chnum verbunden” (MK-XXII., Helck, LÄ IV 125). ● Meaning and origin unknown. ■ 1. S. Wenig (1970, 141) suspects in the name, which occurs in or south of Elephantine, “eine einheimische Gottheit ”, which “von der ansäs- sigen Bewölkerung verehrt wurde, aber auch . . . Eingang in ägyptische Tempel mit lokaler Bedeutung fand ”. Henceforth, he identified mjk.t “mit Vorbehalt” with Meroitic mkdj “Göttin” (“aus mk ‘Gott’ und kdj ‘Frau’ kontaminiert”), which was later personified. Accepting this theory, Handoussa (1987, 101–5) saw in this “egyptianized” name (perhaps mjktj?) a “vivid example” of a local divinity, which “the theologians of Egyptianized Nubia tried to interrelate . . . with the Egyptian pantheon”. ■ 2. O. D. Berlev (1978, 58–59 quoted apud AL 78.1668 leaving Wenig l.c. unmentioned): the lit. meaning of the name was conceived as *mj-k.t “semblable à l’autre (main du dieu)” (cf. Habachi, MDAIK 24, 1969, 169f.).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: For listing its exx. cf. also Habachi (in MDAIK 24, 1969, 177f.), Wenig (1970, 141), and Handoussa (1987, 102, fn. 1).

text: mjk3.t “eine offizinell verwendete Frucht” (Med., Wb II 45, 2) = “(Einzeldroge in einem Verband, unbekannt)” (WÄDN 225) = “ein Mineral” (GHWb 326) = “(Frucht/Mineral?)” (HAM 582). ● Meaning and origin obscure.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: V. Loret (1894, 94–95, §xiii) identified it with a certain Cpt. ⲉⲙⲕⲏ, ⲙ̄ⲕⲏ “Anis, Pimpinella Anisum L.” (Peyron after Tattam, not attested in CD, KHW, DELC etc.), a plant introduced to Egypt at the beginning of Dyn. XVIII.

text: mjtr “als Titel” (OK, CT, MK, XXVI., Wb II 45, 4–5) = “Arbeiter am kgl. Hofe, der zu Beginn der 5. Dyn. beseitigt wird” (Helck 1954, 102: since II./III.) = “a kind of worker in the royal court” (MK, Ward 1982, 94, §790) = “Palastarbeiter” (GHWb 326) = “a palace type of servants (a rather frequent title of unknown signification)” (WD III 50: cf. JNES 18, 1959, 263f.; SAK 10, 1983, 274, n. 5; SAK 23, 1996, 88, n. 22). ● Fem. pair: mjtr.t “als Frauentitel” (OK, Wb II 45, 6) = “mjtr.t-Arbeiterin” (Speidel 1990, 193) = “Palastarbeiter” (GHWb 326) = “lady, concubine” ( Jones 2000, 424–5, §1572). ● Reading, meaning, and origin obscure. W. Helck (1954, 102) explained mjtr from *mjtj-r-t3 and affiliated it with the expression ( j)r( j)-t3 (Helck: “jubelndes Volk im Sedfestritual?”).

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: Not translated in Kahl et al. 1995, 13D & 242 index as well as in Jones 2000, 424, §1571 (with further lit.).

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: W. Helck (1954, 102) read only mtr (sic). G. Roquet (1977, 125, fn. 10; 1979, 447, fn. 2) proposed to read mrtr < m*lt (sic).

text: mjd3 “ein eßbarer Körperteil des Rindes (vom Bein?)” (PT 1546c, offering lists, Wb II 45, 7) = “une partie des jambes (?)” (Lacau 1970 phon., 39, §19) = “chair” (Speelers, p.c. by H. Satzinger on 18 Sept. 1996) = “ein Körperteil vom Rind (als Speise)” (GHWb 326; ÄWb I 516). ● Obscure. Perhaps OEg. mjd3 from *mydr or *mydl. Only guesses are possible: ■ 1. H. Grapow (1914, 23) and P. Lacau (1970 phon., 39, §19; 1970, 149, #406) surmized in mjd3 a form enlarged by m- prefix, although they gave no evidence for it. ■ 2. K. Sethe (ÜKAPT V 499 ad PT 1546c), following the (otherwise unpublished) idea of A. Ember, equated mjd3 (< old *mrd3) with Ar. ma-rdaγ-at- “partie charnue du corps située entre la tête du bras et le sternum” [ BK II 847]. Phonologically untenable (Eg.-3 ≠ Ar -γ). ■ 3. GT: no evident parallels in AA. Still, the following data are noteworthy: (1) ES: Geez maṭarā ~ maṭārā “shoulder(blade)”, cf. Tigre maṭerär “spine” (ES: Lsl. 1987, 373; cf. Rn. 1887, 278) ||| WBrb.: Zng. a-marḏi ~ a-marḏi, pl. a-marḏ-un “dos (de l’homme)” [ Ncl. 1953, 214]? (2) NAgaw: Hamir mīdəl-a “elbow” [ BSW 1995, 4] || ECu.: Tsamay madal-akko (m) “arm muscle” [Sava 2005, 245]? (3) Akk. (OAkk.) mudulum “(meat-meal)” [Gelb 1973, 169] = (OAkk., YB) muddulu ~ mundulu “eine Art Fleisch (mit Füllung??)” [AHW 666] = muddulu “pickled meat” [CAD], which W. von Soden derived from ( jB) muddulu D “etwa: füllen (??)” < madālu “in Salz einlegen” [AHW 1572] = madālu “to salt, pickle meat” vs. muddulu D “to preserve in oil or salt” [CAD m1, 10] = muddulu “konservieren” [ Butz, JESHO 27, 1984, 272–316]. Cf. also Akk. midlu “Pökelfleisch” [ Deller, Assur 3/4, 1983, 33–39] = “pickled meat” [ Watson]? (4) LECu.: Saho malad-á ~ ma�ḍ-á “Lende, Weiche” [ Rn. 1890, 265, 267]. (5) For semantical reasons, NBrb.: Shilh a-madl “joue” [ Mntsr. 1999, 164] || SBrb.: Hgr. ă-mâdel, pl. i-mâdl-iw-en “1. mâchoire, 2. p.ext.: mâchoire inférieure (entière), demi-mâchoire (de droite ou de gauche)” [ Fcd. 1951–2, 1161] = ă-madəl, pl. i-madl-iw-ăn “1. demi-mâchoire inférieure, 2. p.ext.: mâchoire” [ PAM 1998, 209], Ghat a-madel “mâchoire” [ Nhl. 1909, 175] are less promising. (6) EBrb.: Gdm. ụ-madir, pl. midar “1. omoplate” [ Lnf.] is certainly out of question.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Occurs in PT among the following parallels: “upper foreleg” (ḫpš ḥrj), “lower foreleg” (ḫpš ẖrj), “haunches” ( jwʕ.w), mjd3, “thighs” (sw.t), “shanks” (ḫnḏ), “back” (psḏ). R. O. Faulkner (in AEPT 235) left mjd3 untranslated.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Lacau (l.c.), in addition, assumed *mld3 or *mnd3 (!) < *ld3 or *nd3 (!).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Moreover, Sethe (see also KHW 104, fn. 5) considered OEg. mjd3 to be the etymon of Cpt.: (SLB) ⲙⲟⲩⲧ “3. Hals, Nacken, Schulter” assuming a contamination with ⲙⲟⲩⲧ “1. Sehne, 2. Gefäß” (< Eg. mt?).

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: The correspondence of ES *-ṭ- vs. Zng. -d- is irreg.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Cf. also Ug. mdl “a strip of tanned leather (i.e. animal hide or skin treated with oil or salt)” [ Watson 1986, 75] = “part of the harness (?)” [ DUL 527]? W. G. E. Watson (1986, 73–75), having declined the rendering “guide rope” (< √dll) suggested by R. M. Good (1984, 77–81), proposed a comparison of Ug. mdl with Akk. mdl. On the other hand, Akk. madālu (as denom. verb) has been derived inversely from muddulu “eine Art Fleisch” of Sum. origin (OL 2003, 207, fn. 23).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: L. Reinisch (l.c.) linked it to Ar. lṭy: laṭā “affixus fuit”.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Following D. J. Wölfel (1955, 43, #14), H. G. Mukarovsky (1969, 34, #3.6 & 40, #20.2) affiliated the Brb. word with Bsq. matel(a) ~ mathela “carrillo, joue, Backe” and mataria ~ matraila “Kinnbacken”.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: It is cognate with NBrb.: Shilh a-madir “Jäthacke” [Stumme] = “1. Haue, Hacke, 2. Stangengebiß des Pferdes” [ Vcl.], Wargla a-mdir, pl. i-midar “1. sorte de houe, de sape, 2. par ext. omoplate” [ Dlh. 1987, 185], Qbl. a-mder, pl. i-medran “1. rebord d’une porte (seuil), d’une fênêtre, d’un bassin, 2. bois de charpentre, poutre” [ Dlt. 1982, 487] || EBrb.: Gdm. ụ-madir, pl. midar “1. omoplate, 2. houe large à manche court qui forme avec le plan de l’outil un angle très fermé” [ Lan- fry 1973, 206, #978] = o-madir, pl. midar “1. breite Hacke mit kurzem Stiel, 2. Schulterblatt (wegen der Hakenform)” [ Vcl.] || WBrb.: Zng. a̱-mdər ~ e̱-mdər, pl. ə-mdurūn “vers, du côté de . . .” [ Ncl. 1953, 207]. Following Stumme (1912, 125), W. Vycichl (2005, 4) explained the Brb. word from an unattested Phn. *mʕdr “Haue, Hacke” via Punic, cf. also Hbr. maʕdēr “plough” [ KB 609] = “1. ( Jät)Hacke, 2. Pflugschar” [ Vcl.].

gloss: ein eßbarer Körperteil des Rindes (vom Bein?)

text: mʕ “1. in der Hand von . . ., im Besitze von . . ., 2. durch die Hand jemds. → durch jem., wegen etwas, 3. vor jem. (retten, schützen), 4. von jem. (empfangen), 5. von jem. (erbitten), 6. von jem. (s. entfernen)” (OK, Wb II 45–46) = “1. in the hand, possession, charge of, 2. together with, 3. from” (FD 105). ● Etymology disputed: ■ 1. Traditionally (e.g. Wb II 45; EG 1957, 132, §178) explained as a compound prep. consisting of Eg. m “in” + ʕ “hand”, which is widely accepted in Egyptian philology. ■ 2. I. Eitan (1928, 48; 1929, 47, 49), followed by P. Lacau (1913, 219, §451; 1970, 17), compared it with Ar. maʕ ~ maʕa “avec”, cf. also maʕā “ensemble”, maʕiyy-at- “1. propriété conjonctive de la copulative, 2. compagnie, juxtaposition” [ BK II 1125], both projecting to Ar. the same compound as in Eg. m-ʕ. Ar. maʕa is cognate with Ug. mʕ II (adv.) “as one, together” [ DUL 519] (cf. Renfroe 1992, 128) and distantly probably also with NBrb.: Mzg. √m: a-mu [-Ø < *-ʕ reg.] “1. participer à, s’associer à, prendre part à, 2. se joindre à” [ Taifi 1991, 399] ||| SCu.: Ma’a -muʔi [-ʔ- < *-ʕ- reg.] “to copulate” [ Ehret] < AA *m-ʕ “(to be) together” [GT ]. ■ 3. The representatives of the Rösslerian trend (“neuere Komparatistik”) identify Eg. m-ʕ with LEg. m-dj “with” (q.v.) < m “in” + ʕ( j) var. *dj “hand” in the frames of the hypothetic shift of Eg. ʕ (~ late var. d?) < AA *d. Disputed in EDE I 356 and Takács 2006, 113. ■ 4. L. Homburger’s (1930, 283) equation of Eg. mʕ ~ Peul (Ful) ngam “à cause” is unacceptable.

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: Eitan did not even exclude that the isolated Ar. prep. “may have come over directly from Egypt”. But contrary to Eitan, such an Eg.-Ar. comparison would exclude the inner Eg. etymology of Eg. mʕ.

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: Similarly to Eitan, V. Blažek (2004, 12, §9) assumes in Ar. maʕa (“a formal parallel”, in his view, to Ar. ladā ~ laday “chez, auprès” [ BK II 984] derived in DELC 145 from li- “to” + yad- “hand”) the same construction as in Eg. mʕ (above) and mdj (m “in” + *d “hand”, lit. “at hand”) as well as IE *me-�h(s)ri- “near”, lit. “at hand”, P. Lacau (1913, 219, §451; 1970, 17), in turn, derived Eg. mʕ, Ar. maʕa, and Hbr. ʕim “with” from a common Eg.-Sem. *ʕ “orientation, direction”.

notes.label: nb3
notes.text: The connection of Hbr. ʕam and Ar. maʕa (supported also in GB 594; MM 1983, 180; KB 839) is dubious. On the other hand, J. Aistleitner (WUS 233–4, #2041) affiliated NWSem. *ʕVm “mit, bei” with Ar. ʕan “von, für, mit, zu”. Note that Ar. maʕa has also a var. ʕam (via met.?) in the dial. of Maroccan Huwara (GB 594).

notes.label: nb4
notes.text: Ma’a -muʔi was wrongly affiliated by Ch. Ehret (1980, 159, #52) with Brg. muʕud- “to pommel” and Dhl. muṯuʕ-u<d- “to masturbate” (rendered by Tosco 1991, 143 more correctly as “to pull down the foreskin”) and explained from his SCu. *muʕ(ut)- “to handle lightly (esp. in a sexual sense)”.

notes.label: lit
notes.text: Zeidler 1992, 208; Schenkel 1993, 140; Kammerzell 1998, 35, fig. 14; Satzinger 1999, 146. Etc.

text: mʕ “Badewanne für die Füße” (OK, Wb II 46, 5) = Fußwanne” (GHWb 326; ÄWb I 516). ● AÄG 109, §254: nomen instr. (or loci) of OEg. jʕj “to wash” (OK, Wb I 39).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The etymology of this root is still obscure: (1) GT: probably cognate with Sem. *hyʕ (extension *h-) “to flow out” [GT ]: ESA (Sab.) hyʕ “to flow, run (of water)”, hyʕ “flow of water, libation” [SD 57], Ar. hyʕ I “2. fondre, être en confusion, 3. couler et se répandre (un liquide répandu), 10. vomir”, VI “1. couler, se répandre” [ BK II 1467–8] = I “to fuse (lead), flow, be spread, vomit” [ Dlg.] (Sem.: DRS 404) ||| ECu. *yaʕ-/*yāʕ- “to flow away” [Sasse 1982, 192] ||| SCu. *waʕ- [< older *yaʕ-?] “to spill out, flow” [ Ehret]: Irq. waʕ- am- “to flow, trickle”, Alg. waʕ-amu “river”, Brg. waʕ-amu “well” | Ma’a -wa “to urinate”, also WRift *waʕ- “to vomit” (SCu.: Ehret 1980, 313) < AA *y-ʕ ~ *w-ʕ “to flow” [GT ]. For ECu.-Sem. see Dlg. 1988, 631, #17. Sem. *h- may be a secondary root complement, while in SCu. we may assume an interchange of AA *y- ~ *w-. For the semantic shift “to wash” vs. “to flow”, cf. e.g. PIE *pleu- “rinnen, fließen” > i.a. Gk. πλύνω “wasche”, OHGerm. flouwen ~ flewen “waschen, spülen”, Lith. caus. pláuju “wasche, spüle” (IEW 835–6). (2) O. Rössler (1971, 293) and R. Voigt (1992, 42) equated Eg. jʕj with Ar. waḍuʔa “sauber werden”, nom. instr. mīḍaʔ-at- “Badewanne” (the only attractive example of the supposed correspondence of Eg. ʕ vs. Sem. *ḏ suggested by the Rösslerian theory and disproved in EDE I 363–6).

text: mʕ “Art Schiff” (MK, NE, GR, Wb II 46, 6) = “type of boat” ( Jones 1988, 137, §33) = “1. (M.R.) kleiner Fahrzeug, das als Transportboot eingesetzt wurde, 2. (Ptol.) eine Barke des Horus” (Dürring 1995, 148, 152) = “1. (MK) type of boat (not stated what it was used for), 2. (Edfu) a general term for the barque of the sun god either in the morning or at night” (PL 417). ● Origin obscure. GT: perhaps lit. “vessel”, a nomen instr. < jʕj?

notes.label: nb
notes.text: D. Meeks (1999, 581) corrected the reading of two Edfu exx. (IV 261:4–5, VII 175:9–10) of PL to *mʕr.t, albeit “un bateau de ce nom ne semble pas connu ailleurs”. For the MK attestation cf. Griffith 1898, 56, pl. xxii, l. 13.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: For the semantic shift cf. e.g. IE *pleu- “rinnen, fließen” > *plowó-s “Schiff”: Gk. πλέω “schiffe, schwimme”, πλο,ον “Fahrzeug”, πλύνω “wasche”, πλυνός “Waschgrube” etc. (IEW 835–6).

text: mʕ (GW) “poteau, bille de bois” (NE, AL 77.1661 after Vernus, RdE 29, 1977, 180, n. 7) = “die Bordränder, oberer Abschluß der Bordwand (bilden in der Aufsicht eines Schiffskörpers die Form eines Mundes, ein Lippenpaar)” (Dürring) = “*Holzstangen” (GHWb 326–7). ● N. Dürring (1995, 62) explained it ultimately from Eg. m3ʕ.w “ein hölzerner Teil der Barke” (CT, Wb II 25, 14, see above).

mʕ “to slay, kill” (GR hapax: Edfu III 4:2, PL 413) ● Reduplicated: mʕmʕ “to kill” (GR, PL 415: 5 exx.) = “töten” (Budde & Kurth 1994, 12, §47). ● Etymology disputable: ■ 1. GT: perhaps continues older *m3ʕ, cf. dj-m3ʕ “schlachten” (late NK, Wb II 22, 12), which ultimately derives from Eg. m3ʕ “richtig” (Wb, discussed above, q.v.)? ■ 2. GT: if D. Meeks (l.c.) is right in assuming a distinct Eg. root *mʕ “to kill” (or sim.), cf. perhaps AA *m-ʕ “1. to hit, 2. cut” [GT ].

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Written m3ʕ. P. Wilson (PL): “most likely a corruption of sm3 slay”, declined by D. Meeks (1999, 581) who, in view of its reduplication, rightly assumed an original stem *mʕ.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Budde and Kurth (l.c.) read m3ʕm3ʕ.

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: Attested in Ar. maʕmaʕa “3. lutter, être aux prises les uns avec les autres”, maʕmaʕ-at- “cris, tumulte des guerrieurs ou des hommes engagés dans une rixe” [ BK II 1130] ||| LECu.: Saho maʕ “spalten, zerteilen, offen, öffnen” [ Rn. 1890, 254] || SCu.: WRift *muʕ- “to beat” [ KM 2004, 209] | Ma’a ma “to beat, hit” [ Tucker-Bryan 1974, 205] ||| CCh.: PBata *√m “couper (avec un couteau, une faucille)” [ Brt.-Jng.]: Bcm. má “couper (avec un couteau)” [Skn. apud Brt.-Jng. 1990, 92, 143] = máá “to cut (with knife)” [ Pweddon 2000, 52], Gude ma “couper de l’herbe, faucher” [ Brt.-Jng. 1990, 143].

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: Note that Saho maʕ was combined by L. Reinisch (1890, 254) with a certain LEg. m3ʕ (knife det.).

text: *mʕ3.t (?) > Cpt.: (B) ⲙⲁⲓⲏ, ⲙⲁⲏ, (L) ⲙⲁⲉⲓⲏ “size, age, kind” (CD 156a) = “1. Ausmaß, Größe, 2. Alter, 3. Gestalt, Art” (NBÄ) = “Art, Gestalt, Alter” (KHW 88) = “grandeur” (DELC 109). ● Etymology strongly debated. G. Fecht (1960, fn. 373), J. Osing (NBÄ 322), and W. Vycichl (DELC 109) assumed an etymon *m̆ʕ3ế(y).̆t (Osing) derived by m- prefix from Eg. ʕ3j “to be great,” although, as Vycichl (l.c.) admits, “il est difficile de classer cette formation parmi les dérivations connues”.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Cf. also (S) ⲁⲙⲁⲉⲓⲏ “Art”, (L) ⲁⲙⲁⲓⲏ(ⲏ)ⲥ (f ) “Substanz, Gestalt” (KHW 517).

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: Strangely, the hypothetic Eg. *mʕ3.t [< *mʕr.t or *mʕl.t] coincides with LECu.: Saho maʕal “1. groß, alt werden, 2. angesehen, einflußreich, erhwürdig sein, 3. wichtig sein (eine Sache)” [ Rn. 1890, 256], which must be pure chance.

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: The Cpt. forms were explained very diversely in the lit.: (1) J. Černý (CED 77), correctly, identifies (B) ϭⲓ-ⲙⲁⲓⲏ “to grow in size, increase” (CD) = “wachsen” (KHW) with Dem. (Ankhsheshonqi 6:9) ṯ3j-3mj.t “adult age” (CED 77), cf. Dem. 3mj.t “Seele, Charakter” (DG 5:1) of dubious origin and presumed by Černý to be present also in Cpt. (S) ⲛⲁϣⲧⲉⲓⲙⲉ, ⲛⲁϣⲧⲙ̄ⲙⲉ “obdurate, presumptuous, imprudent” (CD 78b) < Dem. nḫt-3mj.(t) “hard of character” (CED 115). (2) B. H. Stricker (OMRO NR 39, 1958, 61, n. 36), in turn, explained Cpt. from bj3.t “Charakter” (Wb I 441), while (3) A. Volten (1942, 109; 1962, 98) preferred a derivation from Dem. mj.t “Weg, Art” (DG 152).

text: mʕj.t “Öse (für Vorhänge)” (GR, Wb II 46, 8) = “boucle d’attache” (Alliot 1949 I, 327–9) = “anneau (de rideau)” (GR, AL 78.1670) = “1. loop (on curtain, on the small shrine), 2. (Edfu VI 125:1) perhaps some kind of loop on the harpoon through which the rope passed” (PL 413–4). Occurs also in the Tebtunis onomasticon: mʕj “Öse” (2nd cent AD, Osing 1998, 227 & n. d). ■ No certain etymology. ■ 1. GT: if its basic sense was “(sg.) round”, presumably cognate with Sem.: OHbr. *māʕā “Körnchen (des Sandes), Steinchen” [GB 443] = “grain (of sand)” [ KB 609], NHbr. of TTM māʕā (f ) “Grundbed.: etwas Rundes: 1. Kern, 2. kleine Münze, Korn, Maah” [ Levy 1924 III 183–4] = “1. Körnchen, 2. eine bestimmte Münze” [ Dalman 1922, 245] = “(orig. grain of sand) 1. a weight, 2. a (small) coin” [ Jastrow 1950, 813] ||| WCh.: Goemai mai “a ring of iron put around the shaft of a spear (is also put around walking sticks and clubs)” [Srl. 1937, 134]. From AA *m-ʕ “round” [GT ]? ■ 2. GT: less probably, cf. NOm.: Mocha mìʔ-o “handle” [ Lsl. 1959, 39]?

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Beside the reading mʕj.t (preferred in Wb, AL, PL), several GR exx. have no third -j and the fem. -t.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: NHbr. mēʕe(h) “1. die ganze Bauchhöhle des animalischen Körpers, 2. das Kerngehäuse einer Frucht” (explained in Levy l.c. from “eig. etwas Rundes”) hardly belong here. Cf. Sem. *maʕay/w-(at)- “intestines, entrails” [SED I 168, #185].

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Ch. Ehret (1995, 314, #607) combined Mocha mìʔ-o “handle” with Sem. *mʕ “to rub” [ Ehret] ||| SCu. *muʕ-ut- “to handle lightly” (“durative” *t) < AA *-mĭʕ- /*-mŭʕ- “to handle”. Semantically unconvincing.

text: mʕ3ʕ.wj “die beiden Stangen der Leiter” (PT 468, Wb II 46, 8, so also Hornung 1980, 236) = “ein Teil der Leiter, die Sproßen oder die Holmen der Leiter” (Spg. 1895, 99) = “the uprights of the ladder” (AEPT 93) = “die beiden Holme der Leiter” (Kessler, LÄ III 1002 & 1004, n. 8) = “die beiden Holmen (die beiden Stangen der Leiter)” (ÄWb I 516). ● Perhaps from the same root derive also: (1) MK mʕ3ʕ “Planke oder ein anderer Schiffsteil” (Hornung 1980, 236 after James 1962, 62/31)? (2) Dram. Pap. Ramesseum B, ll. 117, 119 (late MK): mʕmʕ3.wj (abbreviated form mʕw) “die beiden Leiterholmen” vs. mʕ3 “Holm” (Sethe 1928, 223, 225, 257) = “part of a celestial ladder erected” (Borgouts quoting Junker 1942, 52–52) = “the clubs” (Borghouts 1971, 202) = “Wurfholz” (Hornung 1980, 236)? Cf. Altenmüller ( JEOL 18, 1964, 273f.). (3) For a possible NK ex. cf. also Janssen (BiOr 25, 1968, 39). ● Origin uncertain. ■ 1. H. Grapow (1914, 23) saw in it an m- prefix form, but the underlying root was not identified. ■ 2. E. Hornung (1980, 236) assume that “lexikalisch besteht wohl ein Zusammenhang” between PT mʕ3ʕ.wj and mʕj3.wt “Wurfholz als Göt- terwaffe” (PT 908e, ÜKAPT IV 184) > ʕmʕ3.w “throw-stick-throwers” (CT V 186a, D. Müller, JEA 58, 1972, 121f.), ʕmʕ3 “Netz oder Wurfholz zum Vogelfang” (NK, Pfortenbuch). Dubious. ■ 3. GT: mʕ3ʕ < *mʕlʕ, perhaps any connection to HECu.: Kmb. muluʔla (?) [-ʔ- reg. < *-ʕ-] “ensete tree trunk” [ Hds. 1989, 58]?

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Or belongs rather to m3ʕ.w “ein hölzerner Teil der Barke” (CT, Wb, q.v.) and its kindred?

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: K. Sethe (l.c.) regarded the fuller var. mʕmʕ3.wj as “eine alte dualische Schreibung” for mʕ3.wj.

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: The rendering by Borghouts and Hornung suggests, however, an identification with PT mʕj3.t “throw-stick” (q.v.).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Or cf. HECu. *merʔe-ta (?) “ensete leaf stem” [ Hds. 1989, 58]?

text: mʕj3.t “Wurfholz (?), Keule (?)” (PT 908e, Wb II 46, 10; also GHWb 327; ÄWb I 516) = “bâton de berger” (Montet 1928, 8) = “Hölzer (?), Wurfhölzer (?)” (PT, ÜKAPT IV 184, VI 130) = “clubs” (Borghouts 1971, 201) = “Wurfholz als Götterwaffe” (Hornung 1980, 236) = “Wurfholz (zum Vogeljagd)” (Osing 1986, 208). ● From the same root (?) via met.: (1) OK ʕmʕ3 ~ ʕ3m ~ ʕmʕ “das Wurfholz werfen” (Wb I 186, 1; GHWb 140; ÄWb I 271) = “to throw” (EG 1927, 498). (2) CT ʕmʕ3.t (with numerous vars.) “das Wurfholz zur Vogeljagd” (Wb I 186, 2; GHWb 140) = “clubs” (Borghouts 1971, 201) = “Wurfholz zum Vogelfang (gegen das sich der Verstorbene in CT V 252 zur Wehr setzt; in CT VI 316 werden feindliche Schlangen damit geköpft)” (Hornung 1980, 236) = “throw-stick” (DCT 72, 162). (3) NK ʕmʕ3 “eig. das Wurfholz zum Vogelfang (wird aber bei Ramses VI. deutlich als Netz mit Gitter-Struktur gestaltet)” (Pfortenbuch, scenes 64 & 66, Hornung 1980, 236), discussed below. (4) GR mʕj3 “Wurfholz” (Tebtunis onomasticon, 2nd cent. AD, Osing 1998, 117 & 119, n. y.). ● Etymology debated. ■ 1. H. Grapow (1914, 23): enlarged by the prefix m-, but he named no simplex. ■ 2. P. Montet (1928, 8) regared PT mʕj3.t as “sûrement nom d’action” of a certain *√ʕw > Eg. ʕw.t “Art Szepter” (Wb I 170, 6) = “sorte de sceptre, bâton de berger” (Montet) which he affiliated with j3ʕ “un terme d’élevage” (Montet) = “(Verbum, Behandlung von Kälbern)” (OK, Wb I 27, 16) ■ 3. E. Hornung (1980, 236), followed by H. Altenmüller (LÄ III 45, n. 34), surmized that “lexikalisch besteht wohl ein Zusammenhang” between mʕj3.wt “Wurfholz” (PT 908e) > ʕmʕ3.w “Wurfholz” (CT V 186a) > ʕmʕ3 “Wurfholz oder Netz” (NK) vs. mʕ3ʕ.wj “die beiden Stangen der Leiter” (PT 468) > mʕ3ʕ “Planke (oder ein anderer Schiffsteil)” (early MK). Dubious. ■ 4. R. M. Voigt (1992, 41) and W. Schenkel (1993, 142) combined Eg. ʕmʕ3 with Sem.: Akk. gamlu “Wurfholz, Krummholz, Bumerang” [AHW 279] || Ug. gml “sickle (?)” [Gordon 1955, 251, #451] = “Sichel” [ WUS #661]. In addition, Schenkel (l.c.) supposed an etymological connection between Eg. ʕmʕ3 and Eg. qm3 “Wurfholz” (NK, Wb V 33, 7). ■ 5. C. T. Hodge (1992, 212) explained Eg. ʕ3m as well as ʕmʕ3.t “throw-stick” eventually from his LL (IE-AA) *l-b > *(hH)-l-Nb in frames of his “consonant ablaut” theory (Hodge 1986). ■ 6. GT: was PT mʕj3.t a nomen instr. of an unattested Eg. *ʕj3 “to hunt (?)” (or sim.), perhaps identical with Ar. ʕyl “chercher une proie (se dit d’une bête féroce)” [ BK II 422]? ■ 7. GT: alternatively, the hypothetic Eg. *mʕ3 “to throw a throw-stick” (hence partial redupl. *ʕmʕl?) could be identified with AA *m-l (var. *m-ʕ-l?) “to throw” [GT ].

notes.label: nb
notes.text: R. O. Faulkner (AEPT 213–4, spell 553, n. 9, cf. AECT III 158, spell 1102, n. 2) read PT 1362b mm.t as prep. m “with” + m.t “throw-stick” assumed to be a corruption of ʕmʕ3.t “throw-stick” (Grapow, ZÄS 47, 133). Rejected by K. Sethe (ÜKAPT V 224) and E. Edel (1970, 23–24).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: R. van der Molen (DCT 72) and J. Osing (1986, 208 & fn. 11) surveyed the following CT vars.: ʕmʕ3.t (I 269h, V 252a) ~ jmjʕ.t (II 153f ) ~ ʕmj.w (II 161f ) ~ ʕ3mj.t (II 161f ) ~ ʕmʕ3.w (V 186a, D. Müller, JEA 58, 1972, 121f.: “throw-stickthrowers”) ~ mʕ3ʕ.w (V 186a) ~ jʕm.wt (V 252a) ~ ʕmj3.wt (V 252a, VI 316g, VII 342b) ~ ʕmʕ3.wt (VI 316e, VII 342b) ~ ʕmʕ.t (VII 424b) ~ ʕmj3.t (II 161f, VII 96s) ~ m3ʕ.t (VII 342b, cf. Lesko 1972, 81) ~ ʕm3.wt (VII 520b). The hrgl. depicting a throw-stick (EG 1927, 498, T14) occuring in the wtg. of ʕ3m “Asiatic” from the OK onwards suggests an original *ʕ3m.t “throw-stick”.

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: The corespondence of Eg. ʕ- vs. Sem. *g- is irreg. R. Voigt (l.c.) postulates PSem. *�ml (sic). The interchange Eg. of ʕ ~ q is not justified either by convincing examples.

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: H. Holma (1919, 46) identified Eg. qm3 “werfen” (OK, Wb V 33) with Ar. qamara “mit einem Würfel spielen” [ Holma] = “jouer à un jeu de hasard avec qqn.” [ BK II 810]. G. Takács (2000, 96), in turn, affiliated Eg. qm3 [< either *qmr or *qml] with WCh.: Bokkos kamloŋ “Jadgwurfstock” [ Jng. 1970, 143].

notes.label: nb
notes.text: If, however, PT mʕj3.t was connected to OK ʕmʕ3 “das Wurfholz werfen”, this possibility should be excluded.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Attested in NAgaw *mal “to throw (down)” [Apl.] = *māl “um-, niederwerfen” [GT ]: Xmr. māl [ Rn.] = mal [Apl.], Qmt. māl [CR] = mal- [Apl.], Bln. māl [ Rn.] = mal [Apl.], Dembea māl [ Rn.], Kailinya mal- [Apl.], Xmtg. mal- [Apl.], Qwr. māl [ Rn.] = mal- [Apl.], Falasha māl- [Apl.] (Agaw: Rn. 1884, 392; 1885, 98; 1887, 269; CR 1912, 228; Apl. 1984, 39; 1989 MS, 16; 1996, 18; 2005 MS, 117) ||| WCh.: Bole mall- “1. zu Boden scheudern, 2. flach auf den Boden fallen” [ Lks. 1971, 137] || CCh.: Mofu-Gudur -´məl- “2. lancer (le fuseau)” [ Brt. 1988, 174], Mkt. mùléy “to shoot” & mə̀lá “1. to shoot, 2. throw spear” [ Rsg. 1978, 324, #635 & 346, #742. a] | Puss mili “2. mettre une vêtement, 3. semer” [ Trn. 1991, 106], (?) Mbara màl “laisser” [ TSL 1986, 270] || ECh.: Ngam mál “déchanger, (dé)poser, mettre” & Mobu male “déposer (par terre), mettre” [ Lenssen 1982, 109; 1984, 69].

text: mʕjrt (GW) “Art Frucht (neben Bohnen u.ä.)” (late NK hapax: Pap. Anastasi IV rt. 15:10, Wb II 46, 11) = “unknown word” (Caminos 1954 LEM, 212: perhaps only Pap. Anastasi IV) = “eine Frucht” (Helck 1971, 513, #85) = “sort of fruit” (DLE I 206) = “(a food in a list of foodstuffs after pigeons, honey, goose fat, cream and milk, and before . . . beans, lentils, and peas; it seems to belong to the latter group of grains and legumes)” (Hoch 1994, 126, #160) = “(in Lebensmittelliste nach Tauben, Honig, Gänsefett, Sahne und Milch, vor Körnern und Gemüsen)” (Snd. 1996, 176, #160). ● Apparenly a foreign word. Origin obscure. ■ 1. J. Hoch (1994, 126, #160) abstained from identifying it either with Ar. mīr-at- “provisions” or Talmudic Aram. millat “acorns (used in tanning)”, correctly. ■ 2. Th. Schneider (1996, 176, #160): borrowed from some Anatolian lg., cf. Hitt. milit, Luvi mallit, Palaic malit “honey”. False, since -ʕ- remains unexplained, and the list already has “honey” before our word (signified by a native term).

mʕʕ (bodily efflux det.) “etwas vor dem man sich hüten soll” (XVIII. Mag. hapax: Mutter und Kind 4:1, Wb II 46, 12) = “etwas vor dem man sich hüten muß (in Zshg. mit Lippen)” (GHWb 327). ● Meaning and etymology obscure. With respect to its det. (Aa2) and the connection to lips, Sem.: Akk. mâʔu (a/jB) “(Galle) erbrechen” [AHW 637] = mâʔu “to vomit (bile)” [CAD m1, 437] || Ug. √myʕ: Gt t-mtʕ “to soak in water” [ Tropper 2000, 521–2; Watson 2003, 93] | JNAram. myʔ [from *myʕ] “to quiver like a fluid, churn, be unstable”, mıyāna “moist, liquidy, soft” [Sabar 2002, 216] | Ar. myʕ: māʕa “couler doucement en se répandant à la surface du sol” [ BK II 1173] = myʕ “mollifier, rendre mou et fluide, enduire de mortier mêlé de paille hachée”, mayʕ-at- “la résine du storax”, mayāʕ-at- “fluidité, liquidité” [ Dozy II 629] = myʕ: mīʕān- “fluidité”, māʔiʕ- “humide (?)”, ʔal-māʔiʕāt-u “les corps liquides, fluides” [ Fagnan 1923, 167] || Geez (from Ar.) miʕā ~ meʕā “oil of myrrh, stacte” [ Lsl. 1987, 325] ||| SCu.: Qwd. maʔa-tuko [-ʔ- reg. < *-ʕ-] “phlegm” [ Ehret 1980 MS, 4] | Ma’a mamìà “mucus” [ Ehret 1974 MS, 45] || SOm.: Hamer máámâ “to spit out seeds” [ Flm. 1990 MS, 6] ||| WCh.: Hausa mííyáú “saliva” [Abr. 1962, 676–7] | Grnt. mì “saliva” [ Jgr. 1989, 187] = mì “saliva, spittle” [ Haruna 1992 MS, 24] | perhaps NBch. *-mi “ulcer” [GT after Skn. 1977, 47] || CCh.: Zime-Dari miõeʔ “salive” [Cooper 1984, 17] || ECh.: Jegu mi “Rotz” [ Jng. 1961, 115] are worth being considered as possible cognates. From AA *m-y-ʕ “(to emit bodily) fluid” [GT ]?

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: The -âʔ- of Akk. mâʔu “erbrechen” [AHW 637] < *-ayāʕ- (instead of *-êʔ- < *-eyēʕ-) is irregular. In any case, it has hardly anything to do with Akk. (aA) lā muāʔum “nicht wollen” [AHW 665] as supposed by W. von Soden.

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: PBHbr. of TTM nīaʕ “der Schleim, der durch Räuspern, Schütteln, aus der Brust herauskommt” [ Levy 1924 III, 389] = “1. the effort made to remove phlegm, hawking; 2. the phlegm discharged by hawking” [ Jastrow 1950, 906] = “Schleim” [ Dalman 1922, 270] is hardly related, being usually explained from nwʕ “to shake”.

notes.label: nb3
notes.text: From the same biconsonantal root might derive Ar. maʕʕa “fondre, être fondu, liquéfié” [ BK II 1125] || (?) Geez maʕawa “to be humid, wet, moist, supple” [ Lsl. 1987, 328]. The origin of Akk. māʔu “excrement” [CAD m1, 435, 437] is uncertain. Cf. also WCh.: Tangale-Waja mw�� “to squeeze” [ Kwh. 1990, 238].

gloss: etwas vor dem man sich hüten soll

text: mʕʕm3 ~ mʕmʕ3 ~ ʕmʕm3 “(Substantiv)” (NK: Pfortenbuch, scene 64, Wb II 46, 13) = “(Kraftfeld) der Netze, in denen sich die wirkende Zauberenergie befindet” (Hornung 1980, 236) = “*Wurfnetz” (GHWb 327). Cf. mʕmʕ3.wj “die beiden Prügel(schwingen)” (MK: Dram. Pap. Ramesseum, Sethe 1928, 223; Altenmüller 1964, 273). ● Etymology uncertain. ■ 1. E. Hornung (l.c.) surmizes a transformation from an older sense “Wurfholz zum Vogelfang (bei Ramses VI. deutlich als Netz mit Gitter- Struktur gestaltet)”. Moreover, in his view, “lexikalisch besteht wohl ein Zusammenhang” between mʕj3.wt “Wurfholz” (PT 908e, so also Altenmüller 1964, 274) > ʕmʕ3.w “Wurfholz” (CT V 186a) > ʕmʕ3 “Wurfholz oder Netz” (NK) vs. mʕ3ʕ.wj “die beiden Stangen der Leiter” (PT 468b, so also Sethe 1928, 223) > mʕ3ʕ “Planke (oder ein anderer Schiffsteil)” (early MK). Dubious. ■ 2. GT: the coincidence with ECh.: Kera ámàayà “Fischernetz” [ Ebert 1976, 26] may be accidental.

mʕwḥ (OK) > mjwḥ (MK) “das Ruder” (old texts, Wb II 46, 14) = “paddle” (Birch apud Ceugney) = “rame” (Ceugney 1880, 6 after Brugsch) = “Ruderstange” (Müller 1894, 34) = “une sorte de bâton” ( Jéquier 1921, 162, fn. 1) = “oar” (CT, AECT III 203 index; DCT 161) = “Riemen (rowing-oars)” (Dürring 1995, 82) = “Paddel, Rie- men” (VI.: 4x, ÄWb I 516). ● Apparently a nomen instr. with a prefix m-. Etymology highly debated. ■ 1. C. Ceugney (1880, 6) erroneously considered the late orthography mj(w)ḥ and sought the etymon in a certain Eg. jḥ.w “javelines” (Pierret). False. H. Grapow (1914, 23) correctly registered the shift of mʕwḥ (OK) > mjwḥ (MK) and abstained from Ceugney’s derivation. ■ 2. W. M. Müller (1894, 34) explained the OK vars. mʕwḥ ~ mʕḥw ~ mʕḥ from an Eg. Urform *ḥʕ attested as the hypothetic *wḥʕ “Art Schiff: wohl Fischerboot (nur als Schriftzeichen belegt)” (Wb I 348, 2), cf. wḥʕ “Fischer” (PT, Wb I 350, 1) ~ ḥwʕ “altes Wort für Schiff (wohl wḥʕ zu lesen)” (OK, XXVI., Wb III 52, 1) ~ ḥʕ.w “die Flotte” (MK, Wb III 39, 14), which he affiliated (with a remark “ganz unverständlich”) also with ʕḥ “Seil, Strick (der Fähre und am Netz)” (PT, BD, Wb I 213, 15–16). Rather unlikely. ■ 3. G. Jéquier (1921, 162, fn. 1) affiliated it with a certain Eg. mḥḥ.w “bâtons, fourchus, recourbés du haut, dont plusieurs ont une fourche dans le bas” ( Jéquier) = “Krummstab” (Kaplony, LÄ VI 1387: cf. IÄF 996 suppl.), which he derived (as nomen instr.) from Eg. ḥḥj “chercher” assuming for mḥḥ.w an original lit. sense “instruments destinés à sonder le terrain, à chercher la route”, which, however, as Jéquier himself rightly admitted, “ne peut évidemment pas s’appliquer à” mʕwḥ (OK). False. ■ 4. E. Hornung (1963 II, 166, n. 2) identified its supposed etymon *ʕwḥ with the Eg. hapax ḫrw jḥjḥ (Amduat, 10th hour) “ob vom Gesang der Ruderer?” (Wb I 122, 13) = “Taktruf ” (Schott) = “Klang des Ruderns (der Göttermannschaft) oder eher das Geräusch, das die Ruder (mjwḥw) fortgesetzt (vgl. Redupl.) beim Eintauchen machen” (Hornung), which he eventually derived from Eg. jwḥ (Nebenform jwḥʕ) “benetzen, befeuchten, begießen, bewässern, überfluten, befeuchten, sprengen” (since MK, Wb I 57, 1–8) < unattested OK *ʕwḥ. J. Zeidler (1999 II, 325, fn. 2) approved the derivation from MK jwḥ “benetzen usw.”, albeit only if the group mʕ- of OK (!) mʕwḥ stands for m- (as from MK on), i.e., our old word was mwḥ ~ mjwḥ (*m̆ʔwīḥ̆w). Improbable.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: In Amduat, both mʕwḥ.w vs. mjwḥ.w are attested (Hornung 1963 II, 157, n. 4). For further evidence of the shift ʕ . . . ḥ > j . . . ḥ see Vycichl 1990, 254.

text: mʕb3 “Art Speer” (PT, Wb II 47, 1–3, cf. also RdE 15, 1963, 60, n. 1) = “harpoon” (FD 105) = “lance, spear, also harpoon” (Caminos 1972, 219, cf. WD I 85) = “Harpune, (Fisch)Speer” (GHWb 327; ÄWb I 516). ● Identical with Ar. miʕbal-at- “1. fer de flèche long et large, 2. flèche au fer long et large” [ BK II 159] = “a broad and long arrow-head or an iron (iron-head) made broad, an arrow having a broad head” [ Lane 1942] = “arrowhead” [ Lsl.] = miʕbal-at- “arrow with a thick head” [Alb. 1919, 179, #11] = miʕbal-at- “a kind of arrow” [ Ember after Nöldeke 1910, 55] = miʕbal-at- “large arrow point” vs. miʕbal- “cutting tool” [ Frz. 1977, 164] = miʕbal-at- “arrow” [ Vcl. 1983, 108] || Geez māʕəbal ~ māʕəbalt “1. tool, instrument, fittings, 2. arrow, weapon, spear” [ Lsl. 1987, 54] = maʕbal “sharp instrument, arrow” [ Ember] = mabʕal ~ mâ(ʕ)bal “instrument, utensil, weapon” [Alb. 1919, 179, #11] = maʕbal ~ mabʕal “trait, javelot” [Chn.] = māʕbal “telum, jaculum” [ Vcl.] = maʕbäl “arrow” [ Frz. 1977, 164]. The Eg.-Sem. stem *mV-ʕbVl- is apparently nomen instr. (cf. Grapow 1914, 23), but the basic meaning of the underlying Eg.-Sem. *ʕbl is disputed. Most suggestive is Ar. ʕabula “to be(come) large, big, bulky, thick” or ʕabala “to cut (off ) to extirpate it” [ Lane 1941]. ● Other etymologies cannot be accepted.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Goodwin (1867, 95) explained Cpt. (B) ⲙⲃⲁⲓ, (S) ⲙⲡⲁⲓ “a distaff or spindle” (CD 177b: “spindle”) from OK mʕb3 “javelin”, which is usually derived from Eg. nb3 (CED 86).

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: Cf. Ar. miʕwal- “barre de fer pointue avec laquelle on brise les pierres” [ BK II 412] = miʕwal- “a pickaxe or stone-cutter’s pick, the iron implement, a large faʔs-, with which are pecked or hollowed out rocks or great masses of stones” [ Lane 2201] = “Spitzhaue” [Clc.] = “pic” [Chn.] with a shift of -b- > -w-?

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: W. F. Albright (1919, 179, #11), followed later by W. Leslau (1987, 84), combined the Geez and Ar. noun with Akk. (nA, jB) bêlu “etwa: Waffe” [AHW 120], which is uncertain. Following Dillmann, Albrigh derived Ar. miʕbal-at- “arrow with a thick head” from ʕabila “to be thick”.

notes.label: nb3
notes.text: Already Th. Nöldeke (1910, 55) separated Geez māʕəbal “arrow” from Geez mabʕal “instrument”. Following him, A. Ember (1926, 5, #1) treated Ar. miʕbal-at- “a kind of arrow” as a borrowing from Geez māʕəbal “arrow”.

notes.label: nb4
notes.text: P. Fronzaroli (1977, 160–4), in turn, saw the source of Geez maʕbäl “arrow” and Ar. miʕbal- “cutting tool”, miʕbal-at- “large arrow point” in Sem. *ʕbl > Ar. ʕabala “to cut”, ʕablāʔ- “white rock, narrow strip in the blackness of the earth, the stones of which are white”, ʔaʕbal- “white stone or mountain of which the stones are white” [ Frz.], Dathina ʕibāl (pl.) “heaps of corn” [ Frz.] | Sqt. pl. ʕébhaléten “sharp stones”, cf. máʕbher “rock” [ Lsl. 1938, 293, 296], Mhr. ʔaybēl [ Frz.] = ʔáybəl “flint(stone)” [ Jns. 1987, 10] | Geez ʕubāl “hill” [ Lsl. 1987, 54]. Fronzaroli set up two PSem. etymons, namely *ʕabl-at- “a white stone” vs. *ʕibal- “white stones” (supposed source of the name of Ebla), both carrying the basic meaning “a rock of clear, shining appearence similar to flint but coarse-grained, prob. a variety of granite”. In Fronzaroli’s view, the occasional use of this rock as flintstone explains the Mhr. and Sqt. data, while the Ar. reflexes suggest the stone *ʕabl- was used for making baldes and points.

notes.label: nb5
notes.text: The authors of SISAJa I, #96 considered Geez maʕbal to be the met. of Geez mabʕal (lit. “working tool”) explained from Sem. *pʕl ~ *bʕl “make, do”.

notes.label: nb6
notes.text: W. Leslau (1987, 54, 84) assumed in Geez the following scenarios: (1) Geez māʕəbal(t) derives directly from Geez ʕbl II ʕabbala “to make, do” (which Leslau linked to Sem. *ʕml “to work”). (2) Geez māʕəbal(t) is met. of Geez mabʕal ~ mabʕəl “iron tool, axe”, cognate with Ug. bʕl “to make, manufacture, work” [ DUL 203] || ESA bʕl “to work, excavate bedrock (travailler, creuser le soubassement rocheux)” [SD 26].

notes.label: nb7
notes.text: V. É. Orel & O. V. Stolbova (HSED #1768) combined Ar. miʕbal-at- and Eg. mʕb3 with WCh.: Bole ʔum�ul “wegschleudern” [ Lks. 1971, 133] < AA *mi- ʕVbal- “arrow, spear”, which is untenable. Elsewhere, more convincingly Orel and Stolbova (1990, 80, #51) compared Bole ʔum�ul with Ar. nabala “jeter, lancer des traits, des dards”, nabl-at- “une flèche” [ BK II 1187–8]. For Bole ʔum�ul cf. also WCh.: Klr. �ìl “werfen (Stock usw.), bewerfen” [ Jng. 1970, 351] = “to throw” [ Nwm. 1977, 186] | Tng. bal “spear with a long blade” [ Jng. 1991, 70], Kupto bùuléy “werfen, schleudern” [ Leger 1992, 18], Grm. bèel-áalà “to throw” [Schuh 1978, 118] || CCh.: Glavda bal “to throw, cast” [ RB 1968, 13] | Zelgwa mbál “to throw an arrow” [ Brt. 1995, 202], Mada bál “to shoot” [ Rsg. 1978, 324, #635] | Puss bili “lancer, jeter (une seule chose)” [ Trn. 1991, 79], perhaps Mbara vlà [vl- < *bl-?] “jeter” & vùl “lancer, jeter” [ TSL 1986, 280] | Masa bīl “couteau de jet” [Ctc. 1983, 38]. Note that these Ch. cognates are to be distinguished from Ch. *ḅal- “(to shoot an) arrow” [Stl.] (discussed below), which Stolbova (2005, 35) erroneously equated with Ar. nabala.

notes.label: nb8
notes.text: Assuming that Geez māʕəbal “arrow etc.” [ Lsl.] and Eg. mʕb3 are unrelated to any of the above listed forms, the two diverse basic meanings of Geez māʕəbal ~ māʕəbalt “1. tool” vs. “2. arrow” being due to contamination, we cannot exclude a derivation from AA *ʕ-b-l “to shoot” (or sim.) [GT ], cf. WCh.: Hausa ḅíllà “to throw” [Stl. 1996, 27] | Ron *ḅol “schießen” [GT ]: Fyer ḅol, Bks. ḅol, DB ḅol (Ron: Jng. 1968, 12, #143; 1970, 392) || CCh.: Daba ḅàl “to throw (an arrow)” [ Brt. 1995, 225] || ECh.: Sarwa ḅálāw, Gadang ḅālū “lance (de guerre)” (Somray gr.: JI 1993 MS, 8, #144). Note that Ch. *ḅ is reg. < *ʕ/*ḥ/*ʔ/*h + *b. O. V. Stolbova (1996, 27) prefers equating this Ch. root with Ch. *mb-l “to throw” [GT ] (presented above), although the initial labials (*ḅ- vs. *b-) are different.

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: L. Homburger (1929, 168) compared Eg. mʕb3 with Bantu (sic) u-goba “crochet”, while in another paper (1930, 283) she equated Eg. mʕb3 with Ful (Peul) gawal “lance”. Absolutely baseless.

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: H. Satzinger (1999, 376) considered GR mʕb3 as a Graphie of *mʕb and affiliated it with Eg. ʕbb.t > ʕbb “Speer” (MK, NK, GR, Wb I 178, 13) as well as ndb “verwunden” (BD), which he derived from AA *dVp “ausstoßen, werfen”.

text: mʕb3 “30” (OK, Wb II 46, 15), vocalized *máʕba3 (Vrg. 1973 Ib, 32) → Cpt.: (O) ⲙⲟⲡ in ⲙⲟⲡ-ⲧⲓⲉ “35” (Černý & Kahle & Parker 1957, 94) > (S) ⲙⲁⲁⲃ, (A) ⲙⲁⲁⲃⲉ, (B) ⲙⲁⲡ etc. “30” (KHW 87). ● Origin not clear. One of the “hard words”. Presumably enlarged by a prefix m- (as speculatively assumed in Grapow 1914, 23; Černý 1937, 57; DELC 108 without identifying the etymon). ■ 1. W. F. Albright (1918, 92) & A. Ember (1926, 5, #2; 1930, #5.a.20): Eg. mʕb3 < *ʕbr identified with PB Hbr. məʕubbār “passage” [Albright] = “intercalated” [ Ember]. ■ 2. A. Loprieno (1986, 1309): the original meaning of Eg. mʕb3 might have been *“Komplettheit”, which he derived from Eg. ʕb3 “to present, provide” (OK, FD 41) = “ausgestattet sein” (Wb I 177, 5; GHWb 135). Semantically very weak. ■ 3. GT: the primary meaning of Eg. mʕb3 presumed by A. Ember (1926, 5, #2) as *”lunar month of thirty days” finds typological support in NBrb.: Nefusa u-yĕr “30” coming from u-yĕr “lune” [ Vcl.] = u-yér “luna nuova” [ Bgn. 1942, 240] “à cause des 30 jours de mois” (DELC 108, cf. Wlf. 1954, 31). In the light of these parallels, the coincidence of Eg. mʕb3 < *ʕbr ~ *ʕrb (?) with Cu.-Om. *HarP- “moon” [GT ] is highly noteworthy.

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: Cp. also OHbr. *maʕăbār, st. cstr. maʕabăr “1. das Einfahren, Vorübergehen, 2. Ort des Übergangs”, maʕəbbārā “Furt”, JAram. maʕəbbərā “Furt, Fähre”, NHbr. mēʕăbār “pass(age), crossing”, məʕubberet “pregnant”, šānā məʕubberet “leap year (in the Hebrew calendar consisting of 13 lunar months)” (Hbr.: GB 442; Šapiro 1963, 354).

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: This comparison leads us to Sem. *ʕbr “to transgress” [GT ], which is semantically difficult to explain, cf. Akk. ebēru “überschreiten”, ebertu “jenseitiges Ufer” [AHW 182] || Hbr. ʕbr “vorübergehen, überschreiten”, ʕēber “das Jenseitige eines Ufers, Tales, Meeres” [GB 558, 442, 560] || ESA: Sab. ʕbr “to transgress, pass a boundary”, ʕbr-n “other side (?)” [SD 11], Qtb. ʕbr “side” [ Ricks 1982, 170]. Albright guessed whether “can it refer originally to the number of days in a lunar revolution or ‘passage’?”, while Ember surmized that Eg. mʕb3 “perhaps denoted primarily a month consisting of thirty days . . . Eg. mʕb3 has very early lost its original astronomical connotation, and survives only as ‘thirty’ ”.

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: Attested in Agaw *ʔarb- > *ʔarf- “moon” [Apl.]: Bilin arb-á [ Mnh.] = ʔərbá “moon” [Apl.], Hamir arb-á “moon” [ Mnh.], Hamta arb-a “moon” [Apl.], Qwara & Dembea arf-ā “moon” [Apl.], Qmt. arf-a “month” [Apl.] | Awngi árf-á “moon” [Apl.] (Agaw: Mnh. 1912, 236; Apl. 1989 MS, 2; 1991, 8) || HECu.: Sid. (Agaw loan?) arb-ā ~ arf-ā “moon, month” [ Flm.] ||| NOm.: PGmr. *yarf “moon” [GT ]: She erf, Benesho iʔyērp || SOm. *ʔarP- “moon, month” [GT ]: Ari ʔárfi, Hamer arfi, arpi, Dime εrrpo, εrpo, εrfo, ır1o, ırpo (SOm.: Bnd. 1994, 154; SOm.-Cu.: Flm. 1974, 90, #16; 1976, 320).

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: H. C. Fleming (1974, 90, #16) compared the Cu.-Om. root with Sem.: Ug. ʕrp-t “cloud” [ WUS 243, #2102]. Cp. still Akk. urpatu “cloud” [AHW 1432], Hbr. ʕarāpel “dark clouds” [GB 621] ||| Bed. afra “cloud” [ Rn. 1895, 9]. For Ug.-Bed. see Ehret (1995, 353, #694). If Bed.-Sem. *ʕ-r-p “cloud” is related to Cu.-Om. *H-r-P “moon”, we have probably to give up combining the latter with Eg. mʕb3 “30” (Eg. -b- ≠ Sem. *-p-).

text: mʕn “verschönern (von Stöcken) (?)” (late NK Pap. Anastasi IV, rt. 17:3, Wb II 47, 5) = “to embellish” (Caminos 1954 LEM, 216) = “embellished” (DLE I 213) = “verschönern” (GHWb 327). ● As pointed out by H. Grapow (1914, 23) and R. Caminos (l.c.), it derives from Eg. ʕn “schön (sein)” (MK, Wb I 190), whose origin is disputed.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: For a different interpretation cf. Junge 2003, 259, n. 528.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The etymologies offered so far are: (1) A. Ember (1913, 115, #52) suggested an etymological connection with the lost PEg. *ʕ( j)n “eye” quoting parallels like Germ. schön ~ schauen or Hbr. rāʔū “proper, worthy” < Sem. *rʔy “to see”. (2) C. Brockelmann (1932, 102, #14): ~ Ar. pl. ʔa-ʕyān- “die Notabeln”. (3) O. Rössler (1971, 291): Eg. ʕjn (sic) equated with Ar. zyn “verschönern, schmücken”, but there is no convincing evidence for Eg. ʕ ~ Sem. *z (cf. EDE I 357–361). (4) GT: perhaps ~ HECu. *el- “to be better” [ Hds. 1989, 409]? HECu. *el- < *ʕal-? (5) GT: of extra-AA origin? Cf. PCKhoisan *!an “good” [ Baucom 1972, 20]?

text: mʕn “(Hände und Füße) schlagen, Bastonade geben” (XX., Pap. Mayer A, Wb II 47, 6) = “Fesselung” (Grapow 1914, 23) = “twisting of limbs” (Peet 1930, 21) = “a torture applied to witnesses, suspects, and culprits” (Smith 1978, 362) = “to be twisted” (DLE I 216) = “drehen, schrauben” (Helck, LÄ II 279 after Peet) = “(denotes a corporal punishment affecting a criminal’s arms and feet)” (Willems 1990, 34, fn. 29) = “verdrehen (bei der Folter)” (GHWb 327) = “etw. winden, (ver)drehen” ( Junge 1999, 351) = “schlagen” (WD I 85 after Willems l.c.). R. Caminos (1958, 123, §192) found the same word in the Chronicle of Prince Osorkon: [m]ʕn “to beat, bastinado or perhaps twist (as a form of punishment)”. ● Reading and meaning debated. Origin obscure. ■ 1. H. Grapow (1914, 23): enlarged by prefix m- < Eg. ʕnn “umwinden (?)” (PT 425, Wb II 192, 9), which is certainly valid for Eg. mʕnn (cf. the following entry). ■ 2. H. Willems (1990, 34 & fn. 29) read mn and supposed to have found its older etymon in MK mn “to sever (neck as capital punishment)” (stela no. 9 of Sirenput I in the Heqaib sanctuary). Improbable. ■ 3. GT: if, however, the rendering “to beat” is correct, the following AA parallels should be noted:

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The -ʕ- was apparently to be read as certain GW forms (in Pap. Mayer A 3–4 passim, 3:6) betray, therefore mn (proposed in DLE or by Willems) or mnn (Helck, LÄ II 279) can hardly be correct, albeit not to be excluded either.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: As R. Caminos (l.c., fn. 1) rightly states: “the exact meaning of mn or mʕn remains to be determined, at all events, the verb denotes the infliction of some form of physical punishment”.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: H. Smith (1978, 362), W. Helck (l.c.), and R. Hannig (GHWb l.c.) suggest (reading -nn) a direct identification with Eg. mʕnn (q.v.).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The other instance of MK mn occuring in CT VI 162k has been rendered diversely. AECT II 169: a spelling of mnj “to die”; AL 78.1703 and Willems: “être séparé”; Barguet (1986, 343): spelling of mn “to suffer”.

(1) Ch. *m-n “to beat” [GT ] > WCh.: Ngz. mə̀nú “to knock down with a blow, hit sg.” [Schuh 1981, 105] || CCh.: Guley mamunde “schlagen” [ Lks. 1937, 95] | (?) Mada ámmara [-r- reg. < *-n-] “être couvert d’ecchymoses, de traces de coups, être roué de coups” [ Brt.-Brunet 2000, 192]. (2) Ar. maʕala VIII “porter à qqn. des coups de lance, ou percer coup sur coup avec un instrument pointu” [ BK II 1129] ||| NAgaw: Kemant mĭllō “coup donné sur la joue gonflé” [CR 1912, 229], cf. Amh. mĭllo “petit coup appliqué par le vainqueur sur la jouedu vaincu au jeu de l’ak�ndur�” [CR] || LECu.: Afar màlay (m) “managing to kill sb. who has mortally wounded one, beating mercilessly with all on’s strength, scoring a bull’s eye”, malaye “to beat mercilessly, have a good aim, hit a target” [ PH 1985, 162] ||| WCh.: Tangale mal� “to beat” [ Jng. 1991, 118] = mál- “to beat”, mál_ọ “beating” [ Kidda 1985, 208, #268 & 217, #61] || ECh.: Mkl. (t)ìmìlá “2. gifler” [ Jng. 1990, 112].

text: mʕnn (or mnn?) “gewunden sein” (XX., Wb II 81, 25) = “gewunden sein (von den geschraubten Hörnern der älteren Widderart)” (Hornung 1963 II, 164, #696) = “gewunden sein (Hörner auf Krone)” (GHWb 327) = “curved (of the downward curving type of horns), basic mng.: twist(ed)” (Hovestreydt 1997, 110, n. o) → Ptol. mʕnn (or mnn?) “περιλαμ1άνω, circulare” (Ceugney 1880, 7 after Pierret) = “herumgewunden sein” (Wb II 47, 7) = “to be wound round” (CED 85) = “tordre, tresser, torsader” (AL 77.1665) = “to be bound” (Smith 1978, 362). ● From the same root: (1) mʕnn “das aus zwei Stricken zusammengewundene Seil” (NK: Pfortenbuch II 14, 61f., 158 etc., Wb II 47, 9) = “das gewundene Seil” (Hornung 1963 II, 164, #696) = “twisted rope” (CED) = “Art Strick” (Osing, LÄ III 948) = “der Doppeltgewundene” (Hornung 1980, 158; Zeidler 1999 II, 167, fn. 2) = “Schlangenseil, aus dessen Windungen die Stunden entstehen” (Pfortenbuch, Kákosy, LÄ VI 1363) = “Seil (aus zwei Stricken zusammengewunden)” (GHWb 327); (2) mnn.wj (written with no -ʕ-) “die beiden Verschlungenen (von zwei Schlangen)” (NK: Amduat II 19, 164, Wb II 47, 8; GHWb 327) = “die beiden Gewundenen (Schlangen)” (Ceugney 1880, 7) = “Doppeltgewundener (eine Gottheit)” (Hornung 1963 II, 164, #696) = “eine verschränkte Doppelschlange” (Hornung 1980, 159); (3) mnn (GW: mʕnjnj) “instrument de torture” (AL 77.1666) = “ein Werkzeug zum Verdrehen der Hände und Füße (?)” (Helck, LÄ II 279) = “screw” (DLE II 218) = “Handgelenkschraube (als Instrument der Tortur)” ( Junge 1999, 351) = “Schraube (als Folterbezeichnungin Grabräuberprozessen” (Zeidler 1999 II, 167, fn. 2); (4) mnn “torsion, twisting” (late 3rd cent. BC, CED 85, cf. Lefébvre 1923–4 II, 23, no. 50:4; Belegst. to Wb II 47, 7) = “tordre (le lin)” (AL 77.1665). ● Hence: Cpt.: (S) ⲙⲁⲛⲓⲛ, ⲙⲁⲗⲗⲓⲛ, ⲙⲁⲗⲓⲗ “band, cord” (CD 176a) = “Band, Schnur” (NBÄ 682, n. 766) = “Biegung, Windung” (KHW 95) derived by H. Smith (1978, 362) directly from NK mʕn (XX., above). This etymology is absent in CED. ● Etymology highly disputable. ■ 1. C. Ceugney (1880, 7) derived mnn from nn (sic), cf. Eg. nn.t “replis (?)” (CT, AL 78.2131) = “coils (?)” (DCT 232), which he considered to be related with nnwḥ (sic) as its “forme élargi” (!). ■ 2. W. Vycichl (1933, 178, #8), J. Osing (NBÄ 209), and J. Zeidler (1999 II, 167, fn. 2) assumed a root mʕnn originating from Eg. ʕnn (rope det.) “umwinden (?)” (PT 425b, Wb II 192, 9; GHWb 144; ÄWb I 271–2) = “1. sich winden, wenden, 2. umwinden” (NBÄ 209) = “to bound up, wind round, surround, coil up” (CT, DCT 73), cf. hence ʕnn.w “coil, ribbon” (CT II 115c, DCT 73) and ʕnn.wj “Bez. zweier Schlangen, die umwinden” (NK, Wb I 192, 10). The latter occurs in Amduat II 19 in connection with mnn.wj (written without -ʕ-). This derivation was apparently abandoned by J. Černý (CED 85) and W. Vycichl (DELC 116) who assume a root mnn. ■ 3. GT: following J. Černý (CED 85) and W. Vycichl (DELC 116) in assuming an original root mnn, we find an alternative etymology represented by Ch. *m-n “to twist” (or sim.) [GT ], cf. WCh.: Grnt. mənni “to turn round”, manni “to squeeze” [ Jgr. 1989, 188] = mə́ní “to turn (round)” [ Haruna 1992 MS, 24] || CCh.: Htk. (Hide) mənda̱ “tordre, serrer” [ Eguchi 1971, 219] | Mafa mín- “filer du coton” [ Brt.-Bléis 1990, 227]. ■ 4. GT: or, Eg. mnn < *mll could be a perfect match of LECu.: Orm. mēl-aḍḍa (intr.) “1. to sprain, 2. strain ( joints)”, mēll-ō “foot or tooth turned in wrong direction”, mēll-annā “turning in wrong direction” [Gragg 1982, 283] ||| WCh.: Tng. malle̱ “to interwine (two: rope, thread, cotton, etc.), cf. malme̱ “1. to put a thread, rope, etc., around an object, 2. embrace, coil (snake)” [ Jng. 1991, 119] || ECh.: EDng. màlìyē “wickeln” [ Ebobisse 1979, 141; 1987, 100], also màlmìlē “sich um etwas oder jmdn. drehen” [ Ebs. 1979, 149; 1987, 79] < AA *m-l-l “to twist” [GT ].

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The exx. of Dyn. XX lack -ʕ-, while the GR one has it combined with m- (EG 1927, 460, G20: phon. value only m-). In the Wb Belegstellen a reading mnn is preferred.

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: The traditional reading mʕnn (Wb, GHWb) is doubtful. It is perhaps influenced by the hypothetical derivation from Eg. ʕnn (below). Both NEg. mnn (GW) “gewunden sein” (Wb) and mnn.wj “die beiden Verschlungenen” (Wb) were written without -ʕ-, in which W. Westendorf (1989, 109) supposes a loss (Schwund, sic!) of -ʕ-. However, both J. Černý (CED 85) and W. Vycichl (DELC 116) transcribed consistently all reflexes of the root as mnn.

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: Vocalized in NBÄ 209, 682, n. 766 as *m̆ʕn�/un̆(y) in the pattern *m̆sḏīm̆w of nomina agentis and instr., hence XX. *ma(ʔ)nīnə (Zeidler 1999 II, 167, fn. 2). W. Vycichl (DELC 116), however, assumed a pass. part. *mannūn.aw

notes.label: nb3
notes.text: Pfortenbuch mʕʕ “Schlangenseil, aus dessen Windungen die Stunden entstehen” (Kákosy, LÄ VI 1363) has hardly anything to do with ʕm.w “Verschlinger” (Hornung 1980 II, 194–5), but may be rather a strongly abbreviated var. of mʕnn, which W. Westendorf (1989, 109) explained with an (unjustified) Lautübergang n > 3 > ʕ.

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: The dissimilation of -n- > -l- was influenced by m- (Osing, LÄ III 948). Or vice versa (*m-l-l > m-n-n due to m-?)?

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: The 2nd sense of Cpt. (B) ⲙⲟⲛⲙⲉⲛ “1. bewegen, 2. flechten, drehen” (KHW 95, 519) = “1. to (be) shake(n), twisted” (CD 176a) = “1. mouvoir, ébranler, 2. tressé ( τρεπτός)” (DELC 116) may be due to a late contamination of two two distinct roots (cf. also Eg. mnmn “to move”, below).

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: Was the similarity of PT-CT ʕnn vs. NK mʕnn pure chance? Was the occasional -ʕ- of NK-GR mʕnn ~ mnn perhaps due to a secondary contamination, a false Volksetymologie?

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: Vycichl (l.c.) equated Eg. ʕnn mistakenly with SBrb.: Hgr. e-qqen, caus. sūγen, habit. sūγūn “umwinden, (ver)binden”. Phonologically incorrect (Brb. *q- ≠ Eg. ʕ-). Moreover, the Brb. root is cognate with Eg. qn “weben (?)” (GR, Wb V 50, 5), qnj. w “weaver” (Edfu, PL 1063, cf. Meeks in RdE 24, 1972, 117, n. 4) ||| WCh.: (?) Angas gyin “to tie (of animals, leather apron, leaves)” [ Flk. 1915] | Tsagu ʔun- “to tie” [Skn. 1977, 44] | Boghom kan “to tie” [ Nwm.], Buli kənnu “to tie” [ Nwm.] || CCh.: Tera gəni “to tie” [ Nwm. 1964, 49, #536], Pidlimdi gÌna “to tie” [ Krf.], Hwona kinàŋ “to tie” [ Krf.], Ga’anda kinənči “to tie” [ Krf.], Gabin kinənči “to tie” [ Krf.], Boka kinà-ḍa “to tie” [ Krf.] | Daba kən “to tie” [ Nwm] = kìr [ Krf.] | Lame kənwa & Misme kan “to tie” [ Nwm.] || ECh.: Tumak koŋ “tordre, courber” [Cpr. 1975, 77], Mokilko kìní “tresser (nattes, cheveux)” [ Jng. 1990, 122] (Ch.: Nwm. 1977, 33, #133; Kraft 1981, #422). See Zhl. 1934, 112 (Eg.-SBrb.); Bynon 1984, 279–280, #45 (Ch.-Brb.); HSED #1546 (Eg.-Brb.-Ch.).

notes.label: nb3
notes.text: Eg. ʕnn is cognate with Ar. ʕanna IV “3. tourner qqn. de tel ou tel côté” [ BK II 377] = “sich abwenden von (ʕan), begegnen” (cf. ʕan “away from”) [ Vcl.], which are presumably ultimately related to Eg. ʕn “umwenden” (MK, Wb I 188–189) = “to turn back, return” (FD 43) ||| Sem.: Akk. enû “umwenden, ändern” [AHW 220] || Hbr. ʕny “to answer, reply”, cf. ʕny nifal “1. to bend, 2. be(come) bowed” [ KB 851–3]. For Eg.-Sem. see Erman 1892, 108; Albright 1918, 229; 1927, #61; Ember 1926, 302, fn. 10; Clc. 1936, #135; Vcl. 1958, 381; Ward 1961, 37, #19; AHW 220; Hodge 1991, 173. In any case, OEg. ʕnn has nothing to do with Brb. *ə-qqəl (from *√wḳl?) “revenir” [ Dst. 1925, 267] as proposed by W. Vycichl (1933, 178, #7).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The Cpt. evidence does not evidently (contra NBÄ 209) reveal whether the root had *-l or *-n.

text: mʕnḫ.t “(in dem Ausruck: ḥrj-tp mʕnḫ.t n.t m3ʕ.t als Beiwort des Horus)” (PT 815a, Wb II 47, 14) = “Art Stütze worauf ein Vogel ruhen kann (?)” (Grapow 1914, 23) = “le longue bâton fourchu (≈ ʕb.t ailleurs) sur lequel avaient coutume de s’appuyer les vieillards” (sic) ( Jéquier 1921, 147–8) = “Gebiet (!), Waffe, Stab” (ÜKAPT VI 130) = “gegabelter Stock” (Osing 1980, 221, 223–4) = “a staff” (AEPT 147, utt. 440, n. 2; Fischer 1978, 159: PT & CT; DCT 162: CT) = “eine Gabel (?)” (Snk. 1999, 88) = “ein Szepter” (PT, GHWb 328; ÄWb I 517) = “ein Stab” (WD I 85: cf. JEA 64, 1978, 159). ● Hence: mnḫ.t “Art Stab” (MK, Wb II 88, 5) = “ein Gabelstab” (GHWb 341). ● Derives from the Eg. root ʕnḫ with prefix m-, though its basic mng. is disputed.

notes.label: nb1
notes.text: Occurs in a pun with ʕnḫ (Sander-Hansen 1948, 11).

notes.label: nb2
notes.text: Rendered by G. Jéquier (1921, 66, fn. 7) in PT 815 as “contrepoids (comme le nom du collier)” (similarly E. Staehelin 1966, 122: “Gegengewicht”), which was firmly disproved by H. G. Fischer (l.c.).

notes.label: nb3
notes.text: G. Jéquier (1921, 147–8) considered its peculiar det. with a forked ending as due to a confusion with the det. of Eg. mnḫ.t “cloth” (q.v.) depicting a “horizontal strip of cloth with two strands of a fringe” (EG 1927, 494).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Via *mjnḫ.t < mʕnḫ.t (for the shift of OK ʕ > MK j under the influence of ḫ cf. Osing 1980; Vcl. 1990, 255)?

notes.label: nb
notes.text: (1) J. Osing (1980, 221, fn. 36 & pp. 223–4): < Eg. ʕnḫ “leben” with no explanation for the semantic shift, while (2) W. Schenkel (1999, 88) assumed a lit. sense “zusammengebundenes (?)” < Eg. ʕnḫ “lier” postulated already by P. Montet (1928, 6). (3) G. Jéquier (1921, 147–8; 1921, 167 & fn. 5) erroneously combined it with Eg. mẖn “Art Stock oder Szepter” (PT, MK, Wb, q.v.) rendered as “un bâton pour se reposer (au course d’une marche)” < Eg. ḫnj “se (re)poser” (sic).

text: mʕnḫ.t > MK vars. ʕnḫ.t ~ mjnḫ.t “Art Troddel als Halsschmuck” (MK, Wb II 47, 11) = “houppe pour les colliers” (Ceugney 1880, 5 after Brugsch) = “le pendant, contrepoids comme le nom du collier” ( Jéquier 1921, 66 & fn. 7) = “une amulette de protection” ( Jéquier 1921, 145–6) = “un ornament” (Montet 1928, 6) = “Gegengewicht (nicht nur Gebrauchs- und Schmuckgegenstand, sondern auch Aus- zeichnung und Kraftträger)” (Staehelin 1966, 122 & fn. 9 after Jéquier) = “back-tassel, counterpoise (of necklace)” (Smith 1979, 161) = “Troddel, Quaste” (VI., Osing 1980, 221–3) = “pendentif ” (Vcl. 1990, 255) = “counterpoise (acting as a protector of the body of the king and making his limbs healthy and live)” (PL 416). ● Derives from the Eg. root ʕnḫ with prefix m- (Grapow 1914, 23), though its basic mng. is disputed.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: For later vars. mjnḫ.t ~ m3ḫ.t cf. Fecht 1974, 197 (with further lit.).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: (1) Usually explained from Eg. ʕnḫ “to live”. Thus, e.g., C. Ceugney (1880, 5): lit. “amulette préservatrice pour l’autre vie”; G. Jéquier (1921, 66; 1921, 145–6): act. “ornament pour vivre, pour la vie (terme qui convient à une amulette de protection)” (falsely rendering the prep. m as “for”); H. Smith (1979, 161): lit. “that by which one is kept alive”, followed by P. Wilson (PL 416). So also E. Staehelin (l.c.) and J. Osing (l.c., esp. p. 221, fn. 36) failing to explain the semantic shift. (2) P. Montet (1928, 6), in turn, derived it from a hypothetic Eg. *ʕnḫ “lier” based on ʕnḫ “bouquet, bandeau” and ʕnḫ “serment, jurer (en effet un lien)”. Cf. also Schenkel 1999, 88.

text: mʕnd.t “ das Schiff der Sonne am Morgen und am Tage” (PT, Wb II 48, 1–8) = “day-bark of sun-god” (FD 105) = “evening boat” (PL 415) = “Tagesbarke, Morgenbarke (des Sonnengottes Re)” (ÄWb I 517). ● Nom. loci of ʕnḏ, although it is disputable which Eg. root ʕnḏ in fact underlies. ■ 1. H. Grapow (1914, 23) etc.: < ʕnḏ.w “Sonnenglanz” (OK, Wb I 207, 13) = “dawn” (FD 45). ■ 2. W. F. Albright (1917, 34) and P. Wilson (PL 415) derived mʕnḏ.t from Eg. ʕḏ “wohlbehalten sein” (MK, Wb I 237–8) = “to be safe, become whole” (FD 51), based on the parallelism with Eg. msk.t.t “night-bark of the sun-god” < skj “to perish” (cf. Akk. šalām šamši “sun-set”, lit. “death of the sun”). Less probable, since an orig. Eg. *ʕnḏ cannot be proven.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: Cf. mḏtn (sic) “boat” in CT VII 488f, which Lesko (1972, 34, 145) supposes to stand for mʕnḏ.t.

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The origin of this root is not clear. Most recently falsely compared with CCh.: Fali unǯu “sun” [Str. 1910, 460] | Buduma āǯí “sun” [ Lks. 1939, 90] = àǯí [Cyffer] | Mbara nǯà: “day” [ TSL 1986, 292] || ECh.: Kera ǯè “Tag verbringen” [ Ebert 1976, 59] | Kabalay ǯè “day” [Cpr.] | Tumak nǯā “day” [Cpr. 1975, 88], Ndam ǯów “sun” [ Jng.], Gadang & Sarwa ǯa “sun” [ Jng.] (Ch.: JI 1994 II, 313). See Blz. 1996, 135 (Eg.-ECh.); OS 1992, 189 and HSED #1141 (Eg.-Mbara-ECh.); Sts. etc. 1995, 27 (Eg.-CCh.-Tumak). Phonologically unconvincing (OEg. ḏ ≠ ECh. *ǯ probably < *d).

notes.label: nb
notes.text: The etymology of OEg. ʕḏ (or *ʕnḏ?) is debated.
